front: In the cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system, phospholipase C catalyzes the breakdown of PIP2 into [___] and [___].
back:
• Inositol triphosphate (IP3): Mobilizes calcium from mitochondria and ER.
• Diacylglycerol (DAG): Activates protein kinase C to phosphorylate target proteins.

category: Explain the mechanism of intracellular signaling after hormone receptor activation
front: An experimental drug increases intracellular Calcium to 10⁻⁵ mol/L. This change triggers cellular responses primarily by activating the [___] system.
back:
• Calcium-Calmodulin system.
• Calcium binds to calmodulin, inducing a conformational change.
• This activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinases to phosphorylate specific proteins.

category: Explain the mechanism of intracellular signaling after hormone receptor activation
front: Explain how insulin receptor activation leads to increased glucose uptake in skeletal muscle cells.
back:
• Binding causes beta-subunit autophosphorylation and tyrosine kinase activation.
• Insulin receptor substrates (IRS) are phosphorylated.
• Signaling promotes translocation of GLUT4 vesicles to the cell membrane.

category: Explain the mechanism of intracellular signaling after hormone receptor activation
front: Distinguish between the signaling roles of Gs proteins and Gi proteins within the adenylyl cyclase system.
back:
• Gs (Stimulatory): Activates adenylyl cyclase to increase cAMP formation.
• Gi (Inhibitory): Inhibits adenylyl cyclase to reduce cAMP formation.

category: Explain the mechanism of intracellular signaling after hormone receptor activation
front: Identify the specific second messenger used by Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) that differentiates it from most other peptide hormones.
back:
• Cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP).
• It is activated via membrane-bound guanylyl cyclase following hormone binding.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
coreConcept: Structure and Activation Mechanism of Enzyme-Linked Receptors
front: Unlike G protein-coupled receptors that traverse the lipid bilayer seven times, enzyme-linked receptors (such as those for insulin and leptin) typically pass through the cell membrane only [___] time(s).
back:
• Once (single-pass proteins)
• Extracellular ligand binding triggers a conformational change
• This activates an internal catalytic domain or associated enzyme (e.g., JAK2 or tyrosine kinase)
• Results in downstream protein phosphorylation and gene transcription.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Unlike the seven-pass G-protein coupled receptors, the receptors for [___] and Growth Hormone pass through the cell membrane only once and utilize enzyme-linked signaling.
back:
• Insulin
• This receptor possesses intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity upon activation.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: A 10-year-old male presents with extreme short stature but paradoxical elevation of plasma Growth Hormone. This condition, Laron dwarfism, is caused by a defect in which signaling mechanism?
back:
• Mutation of the enzyme-linked GH receptor
• Failure to activate the JAK-STAT signaling pathway
• Resultant inability to synthesize IGF-1 (Somatomedin C)

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Describe the intracellular signaling cascade initiated upon binding of Leptin to its specific enzyme-linked receptor.
back:
• Receptor dimerization
• Activation of associated Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2)
• Phosphorylation of STAT proteins (Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription)
• Initiation of gene transcription

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Contrast the receptor structure and primary second messenger system of Insulin with that of Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH).
back:
• Insulin: Single-pass enzyme-linked receptor; utilizes Tyrosine Kinase/IRS phosphorylation.
• ACTH: Seven-pass G-protein coupled receptor (GPCR); utilizes adenylyl cyclase/cAMP system.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Identify the specific enzymatic activity activated immediately following the autophosphorylation of the beta subunits of the insulin receptor.
back:
• Tyrosine kinase activity
• This leads to phosphorylation of Insulin Receptor Substrates (IRS) to mediate metabolic effects.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: The anterior pituitary hormone responsible for milk production, [___], utilizes an enzyme-linked receptor pathway rather than the cAMP system used by TSH or LH.
back:
• Prolactin
• It signals via the JAK-STAT pathway similar to Growth Hormone.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: An obese patient exhibits hyperglycemia and hyperinsulinemia. Pathophysiology involves the impaired phosphorylation of [___] proteins, which normally link enzyme-linked receptor activation to glucose transporter translocation.
back:
• Insulin Receptor Substrates (IRS-1/2)
• This impairment is a hallmark of insulin resistance in Metabolic Syndrome.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Explain the fundamental difference between the enzymatic mechanism of the Insulin receptor and the Growth Hormone receptor.
back:
• Insulin receptor: Has intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity within its own structure.
• GH receptor: Lacks intrinsic activity; must associate with separate enzymes (JAK2) to signal.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Contrast the metabolic second messenger of Glucagon with the signaling pathway used by Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1).
back:
• Glucagon: cAMP (via GPCR).
• IGF-1: Tyrosine Kinase (via Enzyme-linked receptor), similar to the insulin signaling mechanism.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Enlist four specific hormones or growth factors that utilize enzyme-linked receptor tyrosine kinase signaling as their primary mechanism.
back:
1. Insulin
2. Growth Hormone
3. Prolactin
4. Leptin (also IGF-1 and FGF)

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Unlike the seven-transmembrane G protein-coupled receptors, enzyme-linked receptors typically span the cell membrane [___] time(s).
back:
• Only once
• Extracellular site binds the hormone
• Intracellular site has catalytic activity or binds an enzyme

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: A morbidly obese patient is found to have a genetic mutation preventing the activation of Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2). This condition would directly impair the signaling of which satiety-regulating hormone?
back:
• Leptin
• Leptin receptors are enzyme-linked (cytokine receptor family)
• Signaling requires JAK2 phosphorylation of STAT proteins

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Explain the role of the beta subunits in the insulin receptor complex upon binding of insulin to the alpha subunits.
back:
• Autophosphorylation of tyrosine residues
• Activation of local tyrosine kinase
• Subsequent phosphorylation of insulin-receptor substrates (IRS)

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Contrast the transmembrane architecture of a G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) with that of a Growth Hormone (GH) receptor.
back:
• GPCR: Passes through the membrane 7 times
• GH Receptor: Single-pass transmembrane protein
• GH receptor utilizes associated JAK2 kinases

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Identify the specific intracellular protein family that moves to the nucleus to initiate gene transcription after being phosphorylated by JAK2.
back:
• STAT (Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription)
• Examples include STAT3 used in leptin signaling
• Initiates protein synthesis for physiological effects

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: In the insulin signaling cascade, the translocation of [___] vesicles to the cell membrane is the primary step for increasing glucose uptake in muscle and adipose tissue.
back:
• GLUT 4 (Glucose transporter 4)
• Occurs within seconds of receptor activation
• Facilitates glucose diffusion into the cell

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: A patient presents with features of acromegaly. The hormone responsible for this condition utilizes a receptor that mediates its effects through the phosphorylation of which downstream mediator in the liver?
back:
• Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1)
• Growth hormone (GH) binds enzyme-linked receptors
• Stimulates IGF-1 production via JAK-STAT pathway

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Describe the sequence of events following the binding of Prolactin to its mammary gland receptors.
back:
• Receptor dimerization
• Activation of associated Janus kinases (JAK)
• Phosphorylation of STAT proteins to stimulate milk protein synthesis

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Distinguish between the signaling mechanisms of the ACTH receptor and the Insulin receptor.
back:
• ACTH: Uses G-proteins to activate Adenylyl Cyclase (cAMP second messenger)
• Insulin: Uses enzyme-linked tyrosine kinase (IRS phosphorylation)
• Insulin uses a tetrameric complex; ACTH uses a 7-pass GPCR

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Name four high-yield hormones that utilize Receptor Tyrosine Kinase or associated kinase signaling.
back:
• Insulin
• Growth Hormone (GH)
• Leptin
• Prolactin (also IGF-1 and VEGF)

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Unlike the seven-transmembrane G-protein coupled receptors, the [___] receptor is an enzyme-linked receptor that passes through the cell membrane only once.
back:
• Insulin receptor
  • Growth Hormone receptor
  • Prolactin receptor

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: A 30-year-old female with acromegaly has a pituitary tumor secreting excess Growth Hormone (GH). GH exerts its effects by recruiting which specific intracellular enzyme system?
back:
• Janus kinase (JAK) family, specifically JAK2.
  • The activated JAK2 then phosphorylates STAT proteins to initiate gene transcription.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Explain the general mechanism of action for hormone receptors that function as receptor tyrosine kinases.
back:
• Hormone binds to the extracellular site.
  • This activates an enzyme immediately inside the cell membrane.
  • Intracellular proteins are then phosphorylated to trigger a biological response.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Contrast the transmembrane orientation of the Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH) receptor with that of the Insulin receptor.
back:
• ACTH Receptor: G-protein linked, loops in and out of the membrane 7 times.
  • Insulin Receptor: Enzyme-linked, passes through the membrane only once.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Identify the adipocyte-derived hormone that regulates appetite via an enzyme-linked receptor coupled to the JAK2-STAT3 pathway.
back:
• Leptin.
  • It signals through a homodimer receptor to activate transcription of target genes.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: The functional insulin receptor is a tetramer consisting of two extracellular alpha subunits and two [___] subunits that span the membrane into the cytoplasm.
back:
• Beta (β) subunits.
  • These subunits undergo autophosphorylation to activate local tyrosine kinase.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: A nursing mother produces milk under the influence of Prolactin. If this hormone's receptor—which lacks intrinsic activity—is blocked, name the enzyme it can no longer recruit to function.
back:
• JAK2 (Janus Kinase 2).
  • Prolactin is a cytokine-family hormone that signals through associated enzymes rather than intrinsic ones.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Describe the sequence of events following insulin binding to its receptor subunits.
back:
• Insulin binds alpha subunits.
  • Beta subunits autophosphorylate.
  • Tyrosine kinase is activated.
  • Insulin-receptor substrates (IRS) are phosphorylated, triggering glucose transport and protein synthesis.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Distinguish between the signaling mechanisms of Insulin-like Growth Factor-1 (IGF-1) and Glucagon.
back:
• IGF-1: Uses enzyme-linked receptor tyrosine kinases.
  • Glucagon: Uses the Adenylyl Cyclase-cAMP second messenger system.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: List three hormones or growth factors that specifically utilize receptor tyrosine kinase signaling.
back:
• Insulin
  • Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF)
  • Hepatocyte Growth Factor (HGF)

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: The metabolic hormone secreted by the pancreas that utilizes an enzyme-linked receptor with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity is [___].
back:
Insulin.
* Binds to alpha subunits on the cell exterior.
* Triggers autophosphorylation of beta subunits.
* Activates insulin-receptor substrates (IRS) to mediate glucose uptake.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: A 35-year-old male with acromegaly has excessive secretion of a hormone that signals via the JAK2/STAT pathway. This hormone is [___].
back:
Growth Hormone (GH).
* Utilizes JAK2 associated tyrosine kinases.
* Induces phosphorylation of STAT proteins.
* Stimulates liver production of IGF-1.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Explain the intracellular signaling steps initiated after Leptin binds to its enzyme-linked receptor.
back:
Leptin signaling sequence:
* Binding causes receptor dimerization.
* Activates Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2).
* Phosphorylates STAT3 proteins.
* STAT3 migrates to the nucleus to regulate appetite-related genes.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Contrast the signaling receptor structure of Insulin with that of Growth Hormone.
back:
Structural differences:
* Insulin: Heterotetrameric receptor (2 alpha, 2 beta subunits) with intrinsic kinase activity.
* GH: Single-pass monomeric receptor that dimerizes and recruits separate JAK2 kinases.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: List four peptide growth factors or cytokines that utilize enzyme-linked tyrosine kinase signaling.
back:
Key enzyme-linked factors:
* Fibroblast growth factor (FGF).
* Hepatocyte growth factor (HGF).
* Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).
* Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1).

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: The anterior pituitary hormone responsible for milk production that utilizes the JAK/STAT enzyme-linked pathway is [___].
back:
Prolactin.
* Binds to single-pass transmembrane receptors.
* Signals through associated JAK2 molecules.
* Stimulates transcription of milk protein genes.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: A patient with Laron dwarfism has high GH levels but low IGF-1. Describe the functional defect in this enzyme-linked system.
back:
GH Receptor Mutation:
* Mutation prevents receptor dimerization or JAK2 activation.
* Intracellular signaling is blocked.
* Results in failure to produce IGF-1 despite GH abundance.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Describe the role of autophosphorylation in the insulin receptor signaling cascade.
back:
Autophosphorylation function:
* Insulin binding to alpha subunits triggers beta subunit phosphorylation.
* Catalytic activity of the receptor increases.
* Creates specific docking sites for signaling proteins like IRS-1.

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Contrast G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) and enzyme-linked receptors regarding their membrane-spanning domains.
back:
Domain differences:
* GPCRs: Seven-transmembrane (serpentine) segments.
* Enzyme-linked receptors: Single-pass transmembrane proteins (pass through the membrane only once).

category: Name the hormones that use enzyme-linked hormone receptors signaling
front: Identify the primary transcription factor activated by the JAK2 enzyme in the leptin signaling pathway.
back:
STAT proteins (STAT3).
* Phosphorylated on tyrosine residues by JAK2.
* Dimerize and enter the nucleus.
* Bind DNA to initiate protein synthesis.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Enzyme-linked receptors are transmembrane proteins that, unlike G protein-coupled receptors, typically pass through the cell membrane [___] time(s).
back:
• Only once.
• The hormone-binding site is on the outside.
• The catalytic or enzyme-binding site is on the inside.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: A patient presents with morbid obesity and hyperphagia. Evaluation reveals a mutation in the leptin receptor preventing Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2) recruitment. Identify the primary transcription factors that fail to activate.
back:
• STAT (Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription).
• Specifically STAT3 in the hypothalamus.
• These factors normally initiate gene transcription for energy balance.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Explain the sequence of activation for a receptor with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity, such as the insulin receptor, upon ligand binding.
back:
• Ligand binds to the extracellular alpha subunits.
• This triggers autophosphorylation of the intracellular beta subunits.
• The activated tyrosine kinase then phosphorylates Insulin Receptor Substrates (IRS).

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Contrast the structural and signaling components of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) with enzyme-linked receptors.
back:
• GPCRs: 7-transmembrane segments; Enzyme-linked: Single-transmembrane segment.
• GPCRs: Use heterotrimeric G-proteins (α, β, γ).
• Enzyme-linked: Use intrinsic or associated kinases (e.g., JAK).

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Specify the immediate intracellular consequence of the autophosphorylation of the insulin receptor's beta subunits.
back:
• Activation of local tyrosine kinase activity.
• Phosphorylation of multiple intracellular enzymes.
• Recruitment and activation of Insulin Receptor Substrate (IRS) proteins.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Growth hormone and prolactin utilize enzyme-linked receptors that lack intrinsic enzymatic activity but signal through the [___] family of tyrosine kinases.
back:
• Janus Kinase (JAK) family.
• Specifically JAK2.
• JAK2 activation leads to subsequent STAT protein phosphorylation.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: A child with short stature exhibits high plasma Growth Hormone (GH) but very low IGF-1 levels. Describe the molecular defect in the receptor mechanism.
back:
• GH receptor mutation (Laron Syndrome).
• Failure of the receptor to activate the JAK2-STAT signaling pathway.
• Inability of the liver to produce IGF-1 in response to GH.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Explain how the leptin receptor mediates long-term protein synthesis after JAK2 is activated.
back:
• JAK2 phosphorylates STAT proteins.
• STAT proteins dimerize and translocate to the nucleus.
• They bind to DNA response elements to activate gene transcription.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Distinguish between the insulin receptor and the leptin receptor regarding their intrinsic enzymatic properties.
back:
• Insulin Receptor: Contains intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity.
• Leptin Receptor: Lacks intrinsic enzyme activity.
• Leptin Receptor: Relies on non-covalently associated JAK2 kinases.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Identify the primary signaling proteins phosphorylated by the activated insulin receptor kinase to initiate downstream glucose uptake.
back:
• Insulin Receptor Substrates (IRS-1 to IRS-3).
• IRS activation leads to PI3-kinase pathway stimulation.
• This results in GLUT4 translocation to the cell membrane.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: The enzymatic conversion of cytoplasmic adenosine triphosphate (ATP) into the second messenger cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) is catalyzed by [___].
back:
Adenylyl cyclase.
- Located in the cell membrane.
- Activated by Gs (stimulatory) proteins.
- Leads to activation of Protein Kinase A.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: A patient presents with polydipsia and polyuria. If the underlying cause is a failure of Vasopressin to increase water permeability in the renal collecting tubules, which specific second messenger system is malfunctioning?
back:
Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system.
- Mediated by V2 receptors.
- Results in phosphorylation of aquaporins.
- Causes insertion of water channels into the apical membrane.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Explain the role of Troponin-C or its functional analog, Calmodulin, upon intracellular calcium binding during hormonal signaling.
back:
- Ca²⁺ binds to four sites on Calmodulin.
- Calmodulin undergoes a conformational change.
- This activates/inhibits protein kinases (e.g., Myosin Light Chain Kinase).
- Initiates cellular responses like smooth muscle contraction.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Contrast the intracellular signaling functions of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) and Diacylglycerol (DAG) within the phospholipid second messenger system.
back:
- IP3: Mobilizes calcium ions from mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm.
- DAG: Activates Protein Kinase C (PKC) and provides arachidonic acid for prostaglandin synthesis.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Identify the primary rate-limiting step in steroidogenesis that is stimulated by ACTH via the cAMP second messenger system.
back:
Activation of protein kinase A (PKA).
- Catalyzes the initial conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone.
- Occurs within the mitochondria of adrenocortical cells.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: In the cell membrane phospholipid system, the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2) is catalyzed by the enzyme [___].
back:
Phospholipase C (PLC).
- Attached to the inside projections of receptors.
- Cleaves PIP2 into two messengers: IP3 and DAG.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: A clinician uses an alpha-adrenergic blocker to treat hypertension. These receptors normally mediate vasoconstriction by utilizing which specific second messenger mechanism?
back:
Cell membrane phospholipid system (Phospholipase C).
- Catecholamines (alpha receptors) use this pathway.
- Leads to increased intracellular calcium and smooth muscle contraction.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Outline the amplification cascade initiated by Glucagon in the liver that leads to the activation of phosphorylase a.
back:
1. Glucagon -> Adenylyl Cyclase -> cAMP.
2. cAMP -> Protein Kinase.
3. Protein Kinase -> Phosphorylase b kinase.
4. Phosphorylase b kinase -> Phosphorylase a (Active).
5. Phosphorylase a -> Glycogenolysis.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Distinguish between the second messenger systems utilized by Vasopressin at its two different primary target sites.
back:
- V1 Receptors (Vascular smooth muscle): Phospholipase C (PLC) system.
- V2 Receptors (Renal epithelial cells): Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: List the three most common second messenger systems used by water-soluble hormones to mediate intracellular functions.
back:
1. Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system.
2. Cell membrane phospholipid system (IP3/DAG).
3. Calcium–calmodulin system.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Binding of a stimulatory hormone to its G-protein coupled receptor activates the enzyme [___], which catalyzes the conversion of ATP to cyclic AMP.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase
• Located on the inner surface of the cell membrane
• Initiates the cAMP second messenger cascade used by hormones like ACTH and Glucagon.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: A 45-year-old female with Graves' disease has antibodies (TSI) that stimulate TSH receptors. These receptors primarily utilize [___] as their second messenger to induce hyperthyroidism.
back:
• Cyclic AMP (cAMP)
• TSI mimics TSH by activating the adenylyl cyclase system
• Leads to continuous thyroid hormone synthesis and follicular hyperplasia.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Explain the role of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) in the cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system.
back:
• Mobilizes calcium ions from the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria
• Increases cytosolic calcium concentration
• Calcium then triggers smooth muscle contraction or cellular secretory changes.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Contrast the signaling mechanism of the Insulin receptor with that of the Glucagon receptor.
back:
• Insulin: Uses enzyme-linked receptor tyrosine kinase; involves autophosphorylation and Insulin Receptor Substrates (IRS).
• Glucagon: Uses G-protein coupled receptor (Gs); activates adenylyl cyclase to increase intracellular cAMP.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Identify the enzyme responsible for cleaving phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2) into the second messengers IP3 and DAG.
back:
• Phospholipase C
• Attached to the inside projections of G-protein coupled receptors
• Produces two distinct products: Inositol triphosphate and Diacylglycerol.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: The regulatory protein that binds four calcium ions to undergo a conformational change and activate protein kinases in smooth muscle is [___].
back:
• Calmodulin
• Activated when calcium concentration rises to 10⁻⁶ to 10⁻⁵ mol/L
• Functions similarly to troponin C in skeletal muscle.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: A patient is administered Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) to manage volume overload. This hormone exerts its physiological effects through which specific second messenger?
back:
• Cyclic Guanosine Monophosphate (cGMP)
• Activates membrane-bound guanylyl cyclase
• Differs from the common cAMP system used by most other peptide hormones.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Describe the signaling steps of the Leptin receptor once the hormone binds to its extracellular domain.
back:
• Receptor dimerization activates associated Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2)
• JAK2 phosphorylates STAT (Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription) proteins
• Phosphorylated STATs migrate to the nucleus to initiate gene transcription.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Contrast the primary downstream activators for the cAMP system versus the Diacylglycerol (DAG) system.
back:
• cAMP: Activates cAMP-dependent Protein Kinase A (PKA).
• DAG: Activates Protein Kinase C (PKC), which then phosphorylates many target proteins for the cell's response.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: List three hormones that primarily utilize the Phospholipase C second messenger system.
back:
• Angiotensin II (in vascular smooth muscle)
• Oxytocin
• TRH (Thyrotropin-releasing hormone)
• Also includes alpha-adrenergic catecholamines and vasopressin (V1 receptors).

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Unlike G protein-coupled receptors, enzyme-linked receptors typically span the lipid bilayer [___] time(s).
back:
* Only once
* Known as single-pass transmembrane proteins

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: A patient presents with morbid obesity and a known mutation in the leptin receptor. Under normal conditions, this receptor signals by activating an associated intracellular tyrosine kinase called [___].
back:
* JAK2 (Janus kinase 2)
* Part of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Explain the immediate consequence of insulin binding to the extracellular alpha subunits of the insulin receptor.
back:
* Autophosphorylation of the beta subunits
* Induction of intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity
* Phosphorylation of insulin-receptor substrates (IRS)

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Contrast the intrinsic enzymatic capability of the Insulin receptor with that of the Growth Hormone receptor.
back:
* Insulin Receptor: Possesses intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity in its beta subunits.
* GH Receptor: Lacks intrinsic activity; recruits associated JAK2 kinases to mediate signaling.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Identify the primary intracellular proteins that are phosphorylated by the activated insulin receptor to propagate downstream metabolic signals.
back:
* Insulin-receptor substrates (IRS)
* Specifically IRS-1, IRS-2, and IRS-3 in various tissues

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: In the JAK-STAT signaling pathway used by prolactin and leptin, the activated STAT proteins must translocate to the [___] to regulate gene expression.
back:
* Nucleus
* Function as transcription factors for target genes

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: A child with short stature and elevated GH levels (Laron syndrome) is found to have a mutation in the GH receptor. Explain why this prevents growth.
back:
* Prevents GH-induced JAK-STAT signaling
* Inhibits the production of IGF-1 (Somatomedin C)

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Detail the mechanism by which the leptin receptor dimer initiates transcription after hormone binding.
back:
* Conformational change activates associated JAK2
* JAK2 phosphorylates the receptor and STAT3 proteins
* Phosphorylated STATs dimerize and enter the nucleus

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Contrast the transmembrane structural arrangement of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) with enzyme-linked receptors.
back:
* GPCRs: Seven-transmembrane segments (serpentine).
* Enzyme-linked: Single-pass transmembrane segment.

category: Explain the mechanism of enzyme linked receptors
front: Name the two anterior pituitary hormones that initiate signaling through the recruitment of JAK2 tyrosine kinases.
back:
* Growth Hormone (GH)
* Prolactin

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: In the cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system, the enzyme phospholipase C catalyzes the breakdown of PIP2 into the two products [___] and [___].
back:
• Inositol triphosphate (IP3)
• Diacylglycerol (DAG)

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: A patient with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus has a defect in the V2 receptor signaling pathway. This specific receptor normally mediates water reabsorption in the kidney via which second messenger system?
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Activates Protein Kinase A (PKA)
• Triggers apical insertion of Aquaporin-2 channels

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Explain the role of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) in mobilizing intracellular calcium upon hormone receptor activation.
back:
• Diffuses to the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria
• Binds to ligand-gated calcium channels
• Triggers the release of stored calcium into the cytoplasm

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Contrast the role of Diacylglycerol (DAG) with that of the Calcium-Calmodulin complex in activating intracellular kinases.
back:
• DAG: Directly activates Protein Kinase C (PKC) within the membrane.
• Calcium-Calmodulin: Binds 4 calcium ions to activate calmodulin-dependent protein kinases (e.g., MLCK).

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Identify the common enzyme-linked receptor signaling pathway utilized by both Growth Hormone (GH) and Leptin.
back:
• Janus Kinase 2 (JAK2) pathway
• Leads to phosphorylation of Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription (STAT) proteins

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: The primary second messenger utilized by Atrial Natriuretic Peptide (ANP) to facilitate vasodilation and renal sodium excretion is [___].
back: • Cyclic guanosine monophosphate (cGMP)

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: During a state of acute stress, ACTH binds to adrenal cortical receptors. Trace the rapid intracellular cascade that leads to cortisol synthesis.
back:
• Activation of Gs protein and Adenylyl Cyclase
• Rise in intracellular cAMP
• PKA activation, which converts cholesterol to pregnenolone

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Describe the mechanism by which the Alpha subunit of a heterotrimeric G-protein terminates its own signal.
back:
• Intrinsic GTPase activity of the alpha subunit
• Hydrolysis of bound GTP back to GDP
• Re-association with beta and gamma subunits to form inactive complex

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Contrast the functional effects of Gs and Gi proteins on the adenylyl cyclase system.
back:
• Gs (Stimulatory): Activates adenylyl cyclase, increasing cAMP and PKA activity.
• Gi (Inhibitory): Inhibits adenylyl cyclase, decreasing cAMP and cellular phosphorylation.

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: Enlist the three primary second messenger systems used by water-soluble hormones for intracellular signaling.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Cell membrane phospholipid system (IP3/DAG)
• Calcium-calmodulin system

category: Enlist second messenger mechanisms for mediating intracellular hormonal functions
front: In addition to the adenylyl cyclase-cAMP and calcium-calmodulin systems, the third major mechanism for mediating intracellular hormonal functions is the [___] second messenger system.
back: Cell membrane phospholipid system (Phospholipase C system). It involves the breakdown of PIP2 into Inositol triphosphate (IP3) and Diacylglycerol (DAG).

category: Define second messenger system
front: In the adenylyl cyclase signaling pathway, the intracellular chemical that serves as the [___] is cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP).
back:
• Second messenger
• Relays the signal from the cell surface to the interior
• Activates cAMP-dependent protein kinases (Protein Kinase A)

category: Define second messenger system
front: A patient is administered a hormone that activates Phospholipase C. Name the two primary second messengers produced from the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2).
back:
• Inositol triphosphate (IP3)
• Diacylglycerol (DAG)
• IP3 mobilizes calcium; DAG activates Protein Kinase C (PKC)

category: Define second messenger system
front: Explain the sequence of events that leads to cAMP formation following the binding of a hormone to a Gs-protein-coupled receptor.
back:
• Hormone-receptor binding induces exchange of GDP for GTP on G-alpha subunit
• Activated G-alpha subunit stimulates membrane-bound adenylyl cyclase
• Adenylyl cyclase catalyzes conversion of ATP to cAMP

category: Define second messenger system
front: Contrast the physical properties and primary actions of the second messengers IP3 and DAG.
back:
• IP3: Water-soluble; diffuses to ER/mitochondria to release stored Calcium
• DAG: Lipid-soluble; remains in cell membrane to activate Protein Kinase C
• Both are derived from membrane phospholipids

category: Define second messenger system
front: Identify the enzyme responsible for terminating the second messenger signal by converting cAMP into inactive 5'-AMP.
back:
• Phosphodiesterase (PDE)
• Prevents prolonged or uncontrolled cellular responses
• Often inhibited by drugs like caffeine or theophylline

category: Define second messenger system
front: The protein [___] acts as an intracellular calcium sensor that, upon binding three to four calcium ions, changes shape to activate or inhibit protein kinases.
back:
• Calmodulin
• Structurally and functionally similar to Troponin C
• Mediates effects like smooth muscle contraction via MLCK

category: Define second messenger system
front: A laboratory study observes a hormone causing a rapid surge in intracellular calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum. This hormone likely utilizes the [___] second messenger system.
back:
• Phospholipase C (IP3/DAG) system
• Used by hormones like TRH, GnRH, and Oxytocin
• Involves Gq-protein coupling

category: Define second messenger system
front: Describe how the second messenger system achieves a 'million-fold' amplification of the initial hormonal signal.
back:
• One hormone molecule activates multiple effector enzymes
• Each enzyme produces many second messenger molecules (e.g., cAMP)
• Each second messenger activates multiple kinases, causing a massive enzymatic cascade

category: Define second messenger system
front: Contrast the receptor locations for hormones using second messengers versus those for steroid hormones.
back:
• Second messenger-dependent: Receptors on the outer surface of the cell membrane
• Steroid hormones: Receptors located in the cytoplasm or nucleus
• Membrane receptors trigger rapid signaling; internal receptors alter gene transcription

category: Define second messenger system
front: Define the term 'first messenger' in the context of the endocrine signaling cascade.
back:
• The extracellular hormone itself
• Binds to the specific receptor to initiate the signal
• Does not need to enter the cell to produce a response

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: In the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP second messenger system, the membrane-bound enzyme responsible for converting cytoplasmic adenosine triphosphate (ATP) into cyclic AMP is [___].
back: Adenylyl cyclase. Activated by stimulatory G-proteins (Gs). cAMP acts as a second messenger to activate Protein Kinase A. This triggers protein phosphorylation cascades leading to specific cellular responses.

category: Define second messenger system
coreConcept: Definition and Components of Second Messenger Systems
front: The intracellular signaling mechanism where an external hormone (first messenger) triggers the formation of an internal chemical mediator to execute the physiological response is known as a [___].
back: • Second messenger system • Mediates effects of water-soluble hormones like peptides and catecholamines • Examples include cAMP, IP3, DAG, and Calcium-calmodulin • Amplifies small hormonal signals into powerful cellular responses

category: Define second messenger system
front: The conversion of cytoplasmic ATP into the second messenger cyclic AMP (cAMP) is catalyzed by the membrane-bound enzyme [___].
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase.
• It is activated by the alpha subunit of stimulatory G-proteins (Gs) after hormone-receptor binding.

category: Define second messenger system
front: A patient presents with symptoms of hyperparathyroidism. The hormone responsible (PTH) activates its target bone and kidney cells primarily through the [___] second messenger system.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system.
• PTH binding triggers Gs-protein activation.
• Increased cAMP activates Protein Kinase A to mediate calcium homeostasis.

category: Define second messenger system
front: Explain the mechanism by which the Phospholipase C (PLC) system generates two distinct second messengers from membrane phospholipids.
back:
• PLC catalyzes the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2).
• It produces Inositol triphosphate (IP3) to mobilize intracellular calcium.
• It produces Diacylglycerol (DAG) to activate Protein Kinase C.

category: Define second messenger system
front: Contrast the second messenger systems utilized by Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) when acting on vascular smooth muscle versus the renal collecting tubules.
back:
• V1 Receptors (Vessels): Use the Phospholipase C (IP3/DAG) system for vasoconstriction.
• V2 Receptors (Kidneys): Use the Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system to insert aquaporins.

category: Define second messenger system
front: Describe the critical "amplification" step inherent in the second messenger cascade system.
back:
• A single activated enzyme (like adenylyl cyclase) produces multiple messenger molecules (cAMP).
• Each subsequent kinase phosphorylates numerous proteins.
• This allows minute hormone concentrations to trigger massive cellular responses.

category: Define second messenger system
front: In the calcium-calmodulin second messenger system, the complex initiates intracellular effects only after calmodulin binds to [___] calcium ions.
back:
• Three to four calcium ions.
• Binding induces a conformational change.
• The complex then activates specific kinases, such as myosin light chain kinase in smooth muscle.

category: Define second messenger system
front: A 30-year-old female is diagnosed with Graves' disease. The Thyroid-Stimulating Immunoglobulins (TSI) mimic TSH by chronically activating the [___] pathway.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system.
• TSI binds to TSH receptors.
• Continuous cAMP production leads to excessive thyroxine secretion and thyroid hyperplasia.

category: Define second messenger system
front: How does the activation of cAMP-dependent Protein Kinase A (PKA) specifically result in a physiological cellular response?
back:
• PKA phosphorylates specific target proteins/enzymes.
• This covalent modification changes the protein's functional state.
• Altered protein activity triggers the final biochemical response (e.g., secretion or contraction).

category: Define second messenger system
front: Distinguish the intracellular roles of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) and Diacylglycerol (DAG) after their formation.
back:
• IP3: Diffuses to the ER and mitochondria to release stored calcium ions.
• DAG: Remains membrane-bound to activate Protein Kinase C (PKC).

category: Define second messenger system
front: List three major anterior pituitary hormones that utilize the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP second messenger system.
back:
• Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH).
• Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).
• Luteinizing hormone (LH) or Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

category: Define second messenger system
front: The intracellular molecule that carries a signal from a cell surface receptor to the interior to trigger a biological response is defined as a [___].
back:
• Second messenger
• Examples: cAMP, IP3, DAG, Calcium ions

category: Define second messenger system
coreConcept: cAMP System in Growth Hormone Regulation
front: A patient with suspected acromegaly has elevated GHRH levels. In the anterior pituitary somatotropes, GHRH carries out its function by increasing the concentration of [___].
back:
• Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)
• It activates protein kinases that initiate hormone secretion and gene transcription

category: Define second messenger system
front: Explain how the phospholipase C (PLC) second messenger system generates its primary signaling products.
back:
• Hormone-receptor complex activates a G-protein
• G-protein activates Phospholipase C enzyme
• PLC catalyzes breakdown of membrane phospholipid PIP2
• Products: Inositol triphosphate (IP3) and Diacylglycerol (DAG)

category: Define second messenger system
front: Contrast the intracellular roles of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) and Diacylglycerol (DAG) within the cell membrane phospholipid system.
back:
• IP3: Mobilizes calcium ions from the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria
• DAG: Activates protein kinase C (PKC) to phosphorylate cell proteins
• IP3 focuses on calcium release; DAG focuses on enzyme activation

category: Define second messenger system
front: Identify the specific membrane-bound enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of cytoplasmic ATP into cyclic AMP.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase
• Its activity is stimulated by Gs proteins and inhibited by Gi proteins

category: Define second messenger system
front: In the mechanism of hormonal action involving calcium, the specific protein that undergoes a conformational change after binding 3 to 4 calcium ions is [___].
back:
• Calmodulin
• Once activated, it initiates effects such as activating myosin light chain kinase in smooth muscle

category: Define second messenger system
front: A 30-year-old male with Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus has a genetic defect in the V2 receptor. Which second messenger system is primarily failed in his renal collecting tubules?
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Failure of cAMP prevents aquaporin-2 insertion into the apical membrane

category: Define second messenger system
front: Describe the "signal amplification cascade" that allows a minute amount of glucagon to double blood glucose levels within minutes.
back:
• One hormone molecule activates multiple G-proteins
• Each adenylyl cyclase produces many cAMP molecules
• Each kinase activates multiple subsequent enzymes (e.g., phosphorylase)
• Results in a million-fold increase in product at the final step

category: Define second messenger system
front: Differentiate between the second messenger systems used by Vasopressin (ADH) at its V1 vs. V2 receptors.
back:
• V1 Receptors: Use Phospholipase C (IP3/DAG) to cause vasoconstriction
• V2 Receptors: Use Adenylyl cyclase (cAMP) to increase water reabsorption
• V1 is primarily vascular; V2 is primarily renal epithelial

category: Define second messenger system
front: Name the two primary second messengers utilized by the hormones that regulate serum calcium levels (PTH and Calcitonin).
back:
• Cyclic AMP (cAMP)
• IP3/DAG (via the calcium-sensing receptor for PTH regulation)

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
coreConcept: Primary enzyme of the cAMP second messenger system
front: The membrane-bound enzyme responsible for converting cytoplasmic adenosine triphosphate (ATP) into cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP) upon activation by a stimulatory G-protein is [___].
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase
• It is activated by the alpha subunit of a stimulatory G-protein (Gs)
• Catalyzes the formation of the second messenger cAMP to initiate an intracellular cascade.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A 35-year-old female presents with tachycardia, heat intolerance, and exophthalmos. Pathophysiology involves thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSIs) causing persistent activation of which specific intracellular signaling pathway?
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• TSIs bind the TSH receptor, inducing chronic cAMP production
• This leads to excessive secretion of thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
coreConcept: Protein Kinase A activation and phosphorylation
front: Explain the biological function of cAMP-dependent protein kinase (Protein Kinase A) once intracellular cAMP levels increase.
back:
• Binds and activates protein kinases
• These kinases phosphorylate specific cellular proteins/enzymes
• This chemical modification triggers the cell's ultimate biochemical response to the initial hormone.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the effects of stimulatory G-proteins (Gs) and inhibitory G-proteins (Gi) on the adenylyl cyclase enzyme system.
back:
• Gs: Activates adenylyl cyclase, increasing cAMP production and protein phosphorylation
• Gi: Inhibits adenylyl cyclase, decreasing cAMP levels and reducing downstream cellular activity.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Name three anterior pituitary hormones that utilize the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP second messenger system to stimulate their target organs.
back:
• Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
• Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
• Luteinizing hormone (LH) or Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: In the renal collecting tubules, Vasopressin (ADH) binds to V2 receptors to increase water reabsorption via the [___] second messenger system.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• cAMP activates kinases that cause aquaporin-2 vesicles to insert into the apical membrane
• Increases water permeability and urine concentration.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A patient is treated for acute hypoglycemia with a glucagon injection. Following receptor binding, how does the resulting cAMP cascade ensure a rapid, high-magnitude increase in blood glucose?
back:
• Enzymatic amplification
• One cyclase produces many cAMPs; each kinase activates multiple enzymes
• A few micrograms of glucagon can double blood glucose within minutes.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Describe the specific intracellular mechanism by which GHRH stimulates the release of growth hormone from anterior pituitary somatotropes.
back:
• GHRH binds membrane receptors linked to Gs
• Activates adenylyl cyclase, increasing cAMP
• cAMP increases calcium influx, causing secretory vesicle fusion and GH exocytosis.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the second messengers generated by the adenylyl cyclase system with those generated by the phospholipase C system.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase: Generates cyclic AMP (cAMP)
• Phospholipase C: Cleaves PIP2 into inositol triphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG)
• IP3 mobilizes calcium; DAG activates protein kinase C.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Identify the critical, rate-limiting step in adrenocortical steroidogenesis that is directly stimulated by ACTH via cAMP activation.
back:
• Conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone
• cAMP activates Protein Kinase A
• Kinases stimulate enzymes that mobilize cholesterol into mitochondria for steroid synthesis.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: In the thyroid gland, the stimulatory effect of TSH on follicular cells is primarily mediated by the [___] second messenger system.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Binding to TSH receptors activates adenylyl cyclase
• cAMP acts as a second messenger to activate protein kinase A

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A 45-year-old male with a pituitary tumor presents with high cortisol levels. The anterior pituitary hormone responsible for stimulating the adrenal cortex via the cAMP pathway is [___].
back:
• ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone)
• Specifically stimulates the zona fasciculata and reticularis
• Increases conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Describe the intracellular cascade triggered by Glucagon binding to its hepatic receptor to increase blood glucose.
back:
• Activation of adenylyl cyclase in the hepatic membrane
• Formation of cAMP, which activates protein kinase
• Cascade activation of phosphorylase b into phosphorylase a
• Rapid degradation of glycogen into glucose

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the second messenger systems used by Vasopressin at V1 receptors versus V2 receptors.
back:
• V1 Receptors (Vascular): Phospholipase C (IP3/DAG)
• V2 Receptors (Renal): Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• V2 activation increases water permeability via aquaporins

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Identify the four major hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary that utilize the cAMP second messenger system.
back:
• TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone)
• ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone)
• FSH (Follicle-stimulating hormone)
• LH (Luteinizing hormone)

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) increases renal calcium reabsorption and activates Vitamin D by stimulating the [___] enzyme system in its target cells.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Increases cAMP in osteocytes and renal tubular cells
• Stimulates formation of 1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol in kidneys

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A patient presents with acute hypoglycemia. The hormone that rapidly mobilizes glucose via an adenylyl cyclase-mediated cascade in the liver is [___].
back:
• Glucagon
• Secreted by pancreatic alpha cells
• Direct antagonist to insulin's effects in the liver

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain how GHRH initiates growth hormone release from somatotropes in the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Binds to specific membrane receptors
• Activates adenylyl cyclase system
• Increases intracellular cAMP
• Stimulates calcium influx and hormone exocytosis

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Distinguish the signaling pathways for Catecholamines (Epinephrine/Norepinephrine) acting on alpha versus beta-adrenergic receptors.
back:
• Beta receptors: Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Alpha receptors: Phospholipase C system
• Beta activation generally leads to metabolic or relaxant effects

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Identify the glycoprotein hormone secreted by the placenta that prevents corpus luteum involution via the cAMP system.
back:
• hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin)
• Maintains progesterone and estrogen secretion
• Essential for early pregnancy maintenance

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: In the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP second messenger system, the specific membrane-bound enzyme responsible for converting cytoplasmic adenosine triphosphate (ATP) into cyclic AMP is [___].
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase
• It is activated by the alpha subunit of the stimulatory G protein (Gs)
• Catalyzes the formation of cAMP, the intracellular second messenger

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
coreConcept: Clinical application of cAMP in hyperthyroidism
front: A patient with Grave's disease has thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI) that bind to TSH receptors. Explain the specific intracellular cascade that leads to the excessive secretion of thyroxine.
back:
• TSI binds the TSH receptor, activating stimulatory G proteins (Gs)
• This activates adenylyl cyclase, which increases intracellular cAMP
• cAMP activates protein kinases that trigger thyroid hormone synthesis and release

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Describe the mechanism of signal amplification within the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system that allows minute hormone concentrations to exert powerful effects.
back:
• A single activated receptor activates multiple G proteins
• Each adenylyl cyclase molecule produces thousands of cAMP molecules
• cAMP activates kinases that phosphorylate many target enzymes, creating an exponential cascade

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the second messenger systems utilized by Vasopressin when acting on V1 receptors in vascular smooth muscle versus V2 receptors in renal tubular epithelial cells.
back:
• V1 Receptors: Use the phospholipase C system (IP3/DAG) to increase calcium for vasoconstriction
• V2 Receptors: Use the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system to insert aquaporins for water reabsorption

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain the essential role of the G protein alpha subunit in the initiation and termination of the cAMP signaling pathway.
back:
• Initiation: Exchanges GDP for GTP, dissociates from beta/gamma subunits, and activates adenylyl cyclase
• Termination: Inactivates itself by converting bound GTP back to GDP via intrinsic GTPase activity

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: The primary intracellular effector of the cAMP pathway which phosphorylates specific proteins to alter cellular function is [___].
back:
• cAMP-dependent protein kinase (Protein Kinase A)
• cAMP binds to regulatory subunits to release active catalytic subunits
• Phosphorylates target enzymes to activate or inhibit them

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A patient is administered Glucagon to treat severe hypoglycemia. Explain the specific cAMP-mediated enzymatic steps in the liver that rapidly increase blood glucose.
back:
• Glucagon increases cAMP, activating Protein Kinase A
• This activates phosphorylase b kinase, which converts phosphorylase b to phosphorylase a
• Phosphorylase a promotes rapid glycogenolysis into glucose-1-phosphate

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain how hormones like Somatostatin exert inhibitory effects on target cells through the G-protein system.
back:
• Hormone binds to a receptor coupled with an inhibitory G protein (Gi)
• The alpha subunit of Gi inhibits adenylyl cyclase activity
• This reduces cAMP formation, effectively antagonizing stimulatory hormonal signals

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system with the calcium-calmodulin system regarding their primary activating signals.
back:
• cAMP System: Primary signal is the activation of adenylyl cyclase via G-proteins to produce cAMP
• Calcium-Calmodulin System: Primary signal is the entry of calcium ions (via channels or IP3) which bind calmodulin

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Identify the specific enzyme that terminates the physiological action of cAMP by hydrolyzing it into 5'-AMP.
back:
• Phosphodiesterase (PDE)
• It breaks the phosphodiester bond of cAMP
• Essential for preventing continuous, unregulated signaling after the hormone is removed

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
coreConcept: Adenylyl Cyclase–cAMP Second Messenger System Hormones
front: Endocrine signaling for hormones such as ACTH, TSH, FSH, and Glucagon is primarily mediated by the [___] second messenger system.
back: Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system. Major hormones include ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH, Glucagon, PTH, Calcitonin, hCG, and Vasopressin (V2 receptors). This pathway typically involves Gs protein activation and Protein Kinase A (PKA) stimulation.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: The enzyme Phospholipase C catalyzes the breakdown of the cell membrane phospholipid [___] into the second messengers inositol triphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol (DAG).
back:
• Phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2)
• Found in the inner leaflet of the cell membrane
• Its hydrolysis initiates two diverging signaling pathways.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: A patient experiences vasoconstriction after the administration of Angiotensin II. Identify the specific enzyme activated on the cytoplasmic side of the receptor that mediates this response via the phospholipid system.
back:
• Phospholipase C
• Attached to the inside projections of the transmembrane receptors
• Activated via G-protein coupling.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which Inositol triphosphate (IP3) increases cytoplasmic calcium concentration.
back:
• Mobilizes calcium ions from the mitochondria
• Releases calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum
• Calcium then triggers smooth muscle contraction or secretory changes.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Contrast the primary downstream targets of the two phospholipid-derived second messengers: IP3 and Diacylglycerol (DAG).
back:
• IP3: Targets calcium stores (ER/Mitochondria) for ion mobilization.
• DAG: Directly activates Protein Kinase C (PKC) for protein phosphorylation.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Name the lipid second messenger that serves as a precursor for prostaglandin synthesis after its release from membrane phospholipids.
back:
• Diacylglycerol (DAG)
• Its lipid portion is arachidonic acid
• Provides substrate for local hormones like prostaglandins.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Hormones like PTH and Oxytocin utilize the [___] second messenger system to trigger rapid intracellular responses like calcium efflux or muscle contraction.
back:
• Phospholipase C (Cell membrane phospholipid system)
• Results in IP3 and DAG production
• Distinct from the adenylyl cyclase-cAMP pathway.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: During labor, Oxytocin binds to its receptor to induce uterine contractions. Explain the conceptual application of the second messenger products in this specific physiological state.
back:
• Receptor activates Phospholipase C
• IP3 release increases cytosolic calcium
• Elevated calcium activates the contractile machinery of the myometrium.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Describe how Protein Kinase C (PKC) carries out its function once activated by the phospholipid system.
back:
• Phosphorylates a large number of intracellular proteins
• Changes the activity of specific enzymes
• Leads to the cell's ultimate physiological response to the hormone.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Contrast the signal transduction mechanisms utilized by Vasopressin at V1 receptors versus V2 receptors.
back:
• V1 (Vascular smooth muscle): Uses the Phospholipase C/Phospholipid system.
• V2 (Renal epithelial cells): Uses the Adenylyl Cyclase/cAMP system.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Enlist four major hormones that utilize the Phospholipase C second messenger system as part of their intracellular signaling.
back:
• Angiotensin II (vascular smooth muscle)
• Catecholamines (alpha receptors)
• Oxytocin
• TRH and GnRH.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: The membrane-bound enzyme that is activated by Gs proteins to catalyze the conversion of cytoplasmic adenosine triphosphate into the second messenger [___] is adenylyl cyclase.
back:
• Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)
• Activates cAMP-dependent protein kinases
• Triggers a cascade of biochemical reactions for the cellular response

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A 45-year-old male with a glucagon-secreting pancreatic tumor presents with chronic hyperglycemia. The intracellular mechanism by which glucagon stimulates hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis is via [___].
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP second messenger system
• Activates a protein kinase cascade
• Specifically activates phosphorylase to release glucose-1-phosphate from glycogen

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain the intracellular signaling pathway triggered by Growth Hormone–Releasing Hormone (GHRH) when it binds to somatotropes in the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Activates the adenylyl cyclase system on the cell membrane
• Increases intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP) levels
• Stimulates both immediate GH release (calcium-dependent) and long-term GH gene transcription

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the second messenger systems utilized by Vasopressin (ADH) when acting on vascular smooth muscle (V1 receptors) versus renal epithelial cells (V2 receptors).
back:
• V1 Receptors: Use the phospholipase C (IP3/DAG) system for vasoconstriction
• V2 Receptors: Use the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• V2 activation increases water permeability via aquaporin insertion

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Identify the specific class of adrenergic receptors that exclusively mediate their hormonal effects through the stimulation of the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP pathway.
back:
• Beta receptors (β1, β2, β3)
• Stimulated by catecholamines (epinephrine and norepinephrine)
• Contrasts with alpha-1 (phospholipase C) and alpha-2 (inhibitory cAMP) receptors

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) increases the secretion of adrenocortical steroids by activating protein kinase A, which is the rate-limiting step triggered by the [___] messenger.
back:
• Cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)
• cAMP levels peak within 3 minutes of ACTH binding
• Stimulates initial conversion of cholesterol to pregnenolone

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A patient with primary hyperparathyroidism exhibits bone resorption and high serum calcium. This pathology is driven by Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) using which intracellular signaling system?
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Increases cAMP in osteocytes and osteoclasts
• Stimulates both rapid calcium mobilization and long-term osteoclastic bone resorption

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain the concept of 'amplification' within the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system as used by hormones like LH or TSH.
back:
• A single activated enzyme creates many cAMP molecules
• cAMP activates multiple molecules of the next enzyme in the cascade
• Allows minute hormone concentrations to trigger powerful cellular responses

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the second messenger systems used by Thyrotropin-Releasing Hormone (TRH) at the pituitary level with Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH) at the thyroid gland.
back:
• TRH: Uses the phospholipase C system to release TSH
• TSH: Uses the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• TSH stimulates iodide trapping, thyroglobulin iodination, and proteolysis

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Enlist four major anterior pituitary hormones that utilize the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP second messenger system.
back:
• TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone)
• ACTH (Adrenocorticotropic hormone)
• FSH (Follicle-stimulating hormone)
• LH (Luteinizing hormone)

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Within the cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system, the enzyme [___] catalyzes the hydrolysis of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2) into the second messengers IP3 and DAG.
back: Phospholipase C. • IP3 mobilizes calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria. • DAG activates Protein Kinase C (PKC) to phosphorylate cellular proteins.

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
coreConcept: Effector enzyme in the cAMP system
front: The membrane-bound enzyme responsible for converting cytoplasmic adenosine triphosphate (ATP) into the second messenger cAMP is [___].
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase
• Located on the inner cell membrane surface
• Activated by the stimulatory G-protein (Gs) alpha subunit

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
coreConcept: Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system in Graves' disease
front: A 30-year-old female with Graves' disease has antibodies that bind to TSH receptors, inducing hyperthyroidism. This pathophysiology is mediated by the constitutive activation of which second messenger system?
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• TSI antibodies mimic TSH action
• Causes prolonged stimulation of thyroid hormone synthesis and release

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain the transition of the heterotrimeric G-protein complex from its inactive to its active state upon hormone-receptor binding.
back:
• Receptor conformational change triggers GDP exchange for GTP on the alpha subunit
• Alpha subunit dissociates from beta and gamma subunits
• Free alpha-GTP subunit interacts with adenylyl cyclase

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A patient with a GH-secreting tumor is treated with Somatostatin. Contrast the G-protein coupling of Somatostatin receptors with that of GHRH receptors on pituitary somatotropes.
back:
• GHRH: Couples to Gs, stimulating adenylyl cyclase to increase cAMP
• Somatostatin: Couples to Gi, inhibiting adenylyl cyclase to decrease cAMP
• This allows precise pharmacological suppression of GH

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Identify the biochemical step immediately following the binding of cAMP to the cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA) complex.
back:
• cAMP binds to the regulatory subunits of PKA
• Active catalytic subunits are released from the complex
• Catalytic subunits phosphorylate specific cellular proteins

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: In the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system, the hormonal signal is terminated when the alpha subunit converts its bound GTP back to [___].
back:
• GDP (Guanosine diphosphate)
• Mediated by intrinsic GTPase activity
• Leads to re-association with beta and gamma subunits

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A patient with Central Diabetes Insipidus is given a Vasopressin V2 receptor agonist. How does this drug increase water permeability in the renal collecting ducts?
back:
• Activates adenylyl cyclase increasing cAMP
• Stimulates PKA-mediated phosphorylation of aquaporin-containing vesicles
• Triggers insertion of aquaporins into the apical membrane

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain how the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system differentiates its intracellular action between a thyroid cell and an adrenocortical cell.
back:
• Intracellular machinery is cell-specific
• Thyroid: cAMP triggers T3/T4 synthesis
• Adrenocortical: cAMP triggers steroidogenesis enzymes
• Outcomes depend on the specific proteins phosphorylated by PKA

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the second messenger end-products of the adenylyl cyclase system with those of the cell membrane phospholipase C system.
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase: Produces cAMP
• Phospholipase C: Produces IP3 and DAG
• cAMP activates PKA; IP3/DAG mobilize calcium and activate PKC

category: Explain the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Enumerate four anterior pituitary hormones that utilize the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP mechanism for their intracellular effects.
back:
• TSH (Thyrotropin)
• ACTH (Adrenocorticotropin)
• FSH (Follicle-stimulating hormone)
• LH (Luteinizing hormone)

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: The membrane-bound enzyme that catalyzes the conversion of cytoplasmic adenosine triphosphate (ATP) into cyclic AMP (cAMP) is [___].
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase
• It is activated by the alpha subunit of stimulatory G-proteins (Gs)
• This represents the primary effector protein in the cAMP messenger system.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A 45-year-old male with polydipsia is diagnosed with Central Diabetes Insipidus. The exogenous hormone administered acts on renal V2 receptors via which second messenger system?
back:
• Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system
• Binding to V2 receptors activates Gs proteins
• This leads to cAMP-mediated insertion of aquaporin-2 channels in the collecting duct.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Describe the immediate downstream intracellular events that occur in a thyroid follicular cell after TSH activates its G-protein coupled receptor.
back:
• Activation of adenylyl cyclase increases intracellular cAMP
• cAMP activates cAMP-dependent protein kinase (Protein Kinase A)
• PKA phosphorylates specific enzymes to stimulate thyroxine synthesis and release.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Contrast the second messenger systems utilized by Vasopressin when it induces systemic vasoconstriction versus when it promotes renal water reabsorption.
back:
• Vasoconstriction (V1 receptors): Uses the Phospholipase C system to increase intracellular calcium.
• Water Reabsorption (V2 receptors): Uses the Adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system to increase apical aquaporin insertion.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Enumerate three anterior pituitary glycoprotein hormones that primarily utilize the adenylyl cyclase-cAMP second messenger system.
back:
• TSH (Thyroid-stimulating hormone)
• FSH (Follicle-stimulating hormone)
• LH (Luteinizing hormone)
• All three share a common alpha subunit and use Gs-protein coupled receptors.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: In the adenylyl cyclase–cAMP system, the specific intracellular enzyme that is directly activated by cAMP to phosphorylate target proteins is [___].
back:
• Protein Kinase A (PKA)
• It is also known as cAMP-dependent protein kinase
• PKA triggers the final cellular response by altering protein activity through phosphorylation.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: A patient is administered Glucagon to treat severe hypoglycemia. How does this hormone increase blood glucose levels via the cAMP pathway in the liver?
back:
• Glucagon-induced cAMP activates Protein Kinase A
• PKA activates phosphorylase b kinase, which converts phosphorylase b to phosphorylase a
• This triggers rapid glycogenolysis and enhances hepatic gluconeogenesis.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Explain the integrated mechanism by which Growth Hormone-Releasing Hormone (GHRH) stimulates the release of Growth Hormone from somatotropes.
back:
• GHRH binds to Gs-coupled receptors, activating adenylyl cyclase
• Increased cAMP levels open cell membrane calcium channels
• The resulting calcium influx triggers the exocytosis of GH-containing secretory vesicles.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Distinguish between the signaling pathways used by Catecholamines (Epinephrine/Norepinephrine) when acting on Alpha-2 versus Beta receptors.
back:
• Beta receptors: Couple with Gs to activate adenylyl cyclase and increase cAMP.
• Alpha-2 receptors: Couple with Gi to inhibit adenylyl cyclase and decrease cAMP levels.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use the adenylyl cyclase– cAMP Second Messenger System
front: Identify the primary hypothalamic hormone that utilizes the adenylyl cyclase system to stimulate ACTH release from the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)
• It binds receptors on corticotropes to activate the Gs-cAMP pathway
• This results in the rapid synthesis and secretion of adrenocorticotropic hormone.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
coreConcept: Primary enzyme of the Phospholipid Second Messenger System
front: Some hormones activate transmembrane receptors linked to the enzyme [___], which catalyzes the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2) into two second messengers.
back:
• Phospholipase C (PLC)
• PLC is attached to the inside projections of the hormone receptors.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: A researcher observes that upon binding of Angiotensin II to vascular smooth muscle, there is a rapid mobilization of calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum. This is primarily mediated by the release of [___].
back:
• Inositol triphosphate (IP3)
• IP3 diffuses to the cytoplasm to trigger calcium release from mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
coreConcept: DAG and Protein Kinase C Activation
front: Explain how Diacylglycerol (DAG) initiates cellular responses after the breakdown of cell membrane phospholipids.
back:
• Activates the enzyme Protein Kinase C (PKC).
• PKC phosphorylates multiple proteins to trigger specific cell responses.
• The lipid portion (Arachidonic acid) also serves as a precursor for prostaglandins.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
coreConcept: Differential action of IP3 vs DAG
front: Contrast the physical properties and primary intracellular roles of Inositol triphosphate (IP3) versus Diacylglycerol (DAG).
back:
• IP3: Water-soluble; diffuses through cytoplasm to mobilize calcium from storage organelles.
• DAG: Lipid-soluble; remains in the cell membrane to activate Protein Kinase C (PKC).

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
