front: Enlist the two immediate products formed when Phospholipase C catalyzes the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2).
back:
• Inositol triphosphate (IP3)
• Diacylglycerol (DAG)

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: The lipid portion of diacylglycerol (DAG) is [___], which serves as the primary precursor for the synthesis of prostaglandins and other local hormones.
back:
• Arachidonic acid
• This molecule is released in addition to the second messenger effects of DAG.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: A patient is administered a drug that specifically blocks alpha-1 adrenergic receptors. This intervention will most directly inhibit the activation of which second messenger system?
back:
• Phospholipase C / Phospholipid second messenger system.
• Alpha receptors (catecholamines) utilize this pathway to cause effects like smooth muscle contraction.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Describe the specific mechanism by which the IP3-induced increase in cytosolic calcium leads to physiological effects like smooth muscle contraction.
back:
• IP3 releases stored calcium into the sarcoplasm.
• Increased calcium often binds to Calmodulin.
• This complex activates kinases (e.g., Myosin Light Chain Kinase) to trigger contraction or secretion.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Contrast the types of Vasopressin receptors (V1 vs V2) based on the second messenger system they employ to carry out their functions.
back:
• V1 Receptors: Use Phospholipase C (IP3/DAG) system; located on vascular smooth muscle.
• V2 Receptors: Use Adenylyl Cyclase (cAMP) system; located on renal epithelial cells.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Identify three hormones (excluding Angiotensin II and Vasopressin) that utilize the Phospholipase C second messenger system for their intracellular effects.
back:
• Oxytocin
• Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH)
• Parathyroid hormone (PTH)
• (Also GnRH and GHRH)

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: In the cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system, the enzyme [___] is activated to catalyze the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2).
back:
• Phospholipase C (PLC).
• It attaches to the inside projections of activated transmembrane receptors.
• Catalyzes hydrolysis of PIP2 into two distinct messengers.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: A hormone binds to a V1 receptor in vascular smooth muscle, activating the Phospholipase C pathway. Which specific product is responsible for the subsequent rise in cytosolic calcium?
back:
• Inositol triphosphate (IP3).
• It mobilizes calcium ions from the mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum.
• The resulting calcium surge triggers smooth muscle contraction.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Explain the role of Diacylglycerol (DAG) as a second messenger after it is formed from the cleavage of PIP2.
back:
• Activates the enzyme Protein Kinase C (PKC).
• PKC phosphorylates multiple proteins to trigger the cell's specific response.
• DAG's lipid portion (arachidonic acid) serves as a precursor for prostaglandins.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Contrast the mechanism of action of Vasopressin at its V1 receptors versus its action at V2 receptors.
back:
• V1 Receptors: Utilize the Phospholipase C system to increase calcium for vasoconstriction.
• V2 Receptors: Utilize the Adenylyl Cyclase-cAMP system to increase water permeability in collecting ducts.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: List three hypothalamic releasing hormones that utilize the Phospholipase C (PLC) second messenger system.
back:
• Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH).
• Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH).
• Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH).

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: The Phospholipase C system is initiated when a hormone-receptor complex interacts with [___] type G-proteins in the cell membrane.
back:
• Gq proteins (G-protein q).
• Activation causes the displacement of GDP by GTP on the alpha subunit.
• The activated subunit then stimulates Phospholipase C.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: A patient is given an alpha-1 adrenergic agonist. Describe the primary intracellular signaling cascade that follows receptor binding in the peripheral vasculature.
back:
• Activation of Gq-coupled Phospholipase C.
• Conversion of PIP2 into IP3 and DAG.
• IP3-mediated calcium release leads to vascular smooth muscle contraction.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: How does the Phospholipase C second messenger system facilitate the synthesis of local inflammatory mediators?
back:
• Hydrolysis of PIP2 generates Diacylglycerol (DAG).
• The lipid portion of DAG is arachidonic acid.
• Arachidonic acid is the essential precursor for prostaglandins and leukotrienes.

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Contrast the final intracellular mediators produced by the Adenylyl Cyclase system versus the Phospholipase C system.
back:
• Adenylyl Cyclase: Produces Cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate (cAMP).
• Phospholipase C: Produces Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) and Diacylglycerol (DAG).

category: Explain The cell membrane phospholipid second messenger System
front: Identify the primary membrane phospholipid that serves as the substrate for the production of IP3 and DAG.
back:
• Phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2).
• It is a minor component of the cell membrane phospholipids.
• Cleaved specifically by the enzyme Phospholipase C.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: The hypothalamic hormone that stimulates the release of Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone (TSH) via the phospholipase C (phospholipid) second messenger system is [___].
back:
• Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH).
• It activates phospholipase C, leading to the production of IP3 and DAG to trigger TSH release.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: A 28-year-old female in active labor experiences powerful uterine contractions. The posterior pituitary hormone responsible for these contractions acts on the myometrium via which specific second messenger system?
back:
• Cell membrane phospholipid (Phospholipase C) system.
• The hormone is Oxytocin.
• It increases intracellular calcium to stimulate smooth muscle contraction.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Explain the role of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) in the phospholipid second messenger system after activation by hormones like Angiotensin II.
back:
• IP3 diffuses into the cytoplasm.
• It mobilizes calcium ions from the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria.
• The released calcium then triggers cellular responses like contraction or secretion.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Contrast the second messenger systems utilized by Vasopressin (ADH) when acting on vascular smooth muscle (V1 receptor) versus renal epithelial cells (V2 receptor).
back:
• V1 Receptors: Use the Phospholipase C (phospholipid) system to cause vasoconstriction.
• V2 Receptors: Use the Adenylyl Cyclase–cAMP system to increase water permeability in collecting ducts.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Enumerate the three primary hypothalamic releasing hormones that utilize the Phospholipase C second messenger system to stimulate the anterior pituitary.
back:
• TRH (Thyrotropin-releasing hormone).
• GnRH (Gonadotropin-releasing hormone).
• GHRH (Growth hormone-releasing hormone).

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Catecholamines causing vasoconstriction by acting on alpha-adrenergic receptors utilize the [___] second messenger system.
back:
• Cell membrane phospholipid system (Phospholipase C).
• This increases intracellular calcium in vascular smooth muscle to cause contraction.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: A patient is treated for hypercalcemia. While Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) primarily uses cAMP in the kidneys, it also utilizes [___] as a second messenger in bone cells to mobilize calcium.
back:
• Cell membrane phospholipid (Phospholipase C) system.
• PTH is unique as it can activate both cAMP and Phospholipase C pathways depending on the target tissue.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Describe the mechanism by which Diacylglycerol (DAG) mediates the cellular response in the phospholipid second messenger system.
back:
• DAG activates the enzyme Protein Kinase C (PKC).
• PKC phosphorylates multiple target proteins to elicit the hormonal response.
• DAG's lipid portion (arachidonic acid) also serves as a precursor for prostaglandins.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Contrast the intracellular signaling of Catecholamines when they bind to Beta receptors versus Alpha receptors.
back:
• Beta Receptors: Activate the Adenylyl Cyclase–cAMP system.
• Alpha Receptors: Activate the Phospholipase C (phospholipid) system.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Identify the specific cell membrane precursor that is cleaved by Phospholipase C to generate the second messengers IP3 and DAG.
back:
• Phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2).
• This cleavage is the rate-limiting step in the phospholipid second messenger cascade.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
coreConcept: Hormones of the Phospholipid Second Messenger System
front: Hormones such as TRH, GnRH, and PTH utilize the [___] second messenger system to mobilize intracellular calcium and activate protein kinase C.
back: * Cell membrane phospholipid system (Phospholipase C) * Enumerate Hormones: Angiotensin II (vascular smooth muscle), Oxytocin, GHRH, Vasopressin (V1 receptors), and Catecholamines (alpha receptors).

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: The specific enzyme activated by transmembrane receptors to catalyze the breakdown of PIP2 into IP3 and DAG is [___].
back:
• Phospholipase C (PLC)
  • This enzyme is attached to the inside projection of the receptors
  • It initiates the lipid-mediated second messenger cascade

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: A pregnant woman receives an infusion of Oxytocin to induce labor. Name the intracellular second messenger system utilized by Oxytocin in the uterine smooth muscle and its primary effect.
back:
• Phospholipase C (PLC) system
  • Generates IP3 to mobilize calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
  • Results in increased force of uterine contractions

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Explain the divergent roles of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) and Diacylglycerol (DAG) once they are released into the cytoplasm.
back:
• IP3: Mobilizes calcium ions from mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum
  • DAG: Activates Protein Kinase C (PKC)
  • PKC phosphorylates proteins to trigger the final cellular response

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Contrast the intracellular signaling pathways used by Vasopressin (ADH) when acting on V1 receptors versus V2 receptors.
back:
• V1 Receptors (Vascular): Phospholipase C system (IP3/DAG) causing vasoconstriction
  • V2 Receptors (Renal): Adenylyl cyclase-cAMP system increasing water permeability

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Identify the hypothalamic releasing hormones that specifically utilize the Phospholipase C (PLC) pathway.
back:
• Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
  • Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH)
  • Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH)

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: In vascular smooth muscle, Angiotensin II binds to its receptor to initiate contraction by activating the [___] second messenger system.
back:
• Phospholipase C (PLC)
  • Produces IP3 to increase intracellular calcium
  • Leads to rapid vasoconstriction and increased blood pressure

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: A patient with hypotension is administered a drug that stimulates alpha-adrenergic receptors. Describe the second messenger pathway activated in the target vessels.
back:
• Alpha-1 receptors activate Phospholipase C
  • Increases production of IP3 and DAG
  • Calcium release leads to smooth muscle contraction and pressor effect

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Explain the mechanism by which Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) utilizes the phospholipid system in addition to its primary cAMP pathway.
back:
• PTH activates PLC in bone cells (osteocytes/osteoclasts)
  • Increases cAMP and intracellular calcium simultaneously
  • Dual signaling facilitates rapid calcium mobilization and bone resorption

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Contrast the second messenger systems of catecholamines when they act on alpha-receptors versus beta-receptors.
back:
• Alpha receptors: Use the Phospholipase C (PLC) system
  • Beta receptors: Use the Adenylyl cyclase-cAMP system

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Enumerate the full list of hormones that use the cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system.
back:
• Angiotensin II, TRH, GnRH, GHRH
  • Oxytocin, PTH, Vasopressin (V1)
  • Catecholamines (alpha receptors)

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: The intracellular protein [___] acts as a primary sensor for calcium entry, requiring the binding of three to four calcium ions to initiate cellular responses.
back:
• Calmodulin
• Changes shape upon binding $Ca^{2+}$
• Activates or inhibits protein kinases via phosphorylation cascades

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: A laboratory study observes that smooth muscle fails to contract despite an influx of calcium ions. Molecular analysis reveals a deficiency in the protein that activates Myosin Light Chain Kinase. Identify this protein.
back:
• Calmodulin
• Bridges the gap between $Ca^{2+}$ influx and MLCK activation
• Essential for cross-bridge cycling in smooth muscle

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Explain the role of the Calcium-Calmodulin complex in the activation of the Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK) pathway.
back:
• $Ca^{2+}$ binds to Calmodulin (4 binding sites)
• Complex activates MLCK
• MLCK phosphorylates the myosin light chain
• Facilitates myosin-actin interaction

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
coreConcept: Regulatory Protein Contrast (Calmodulin vs. Troponin C)
front: Contrast the intracellular response of a smooth muscle cell versus a skeletal muscle cell when cytosolic calcium rises to $10^{-6}$ mol/L, specifically regarding their regulatory proteins.
back:
• Smooth Muscle: $Ca^{2+}$ binds Calmodulin to activate MLCK
• Skeletal Muscle: $Ca^{2+}$ binds Troponin C to move tropomyosin
• Both require similar calcium thresholds for activation

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Identify the critical intracellular calcium concentration range required to overcome basal levels ($10^{-8}$ mol/L) and trigger the Calmodulin system.
back:
• $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$ mol/L
• Represents a 10 to 100-fold increase over resting levels
• Matches the threshold for Troponin C activation in skeletal muscle

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: The structural and functional analogue of Calmodulin found specifically in skeletal and cardiac muscle is [___].
back:
• Troponin C
• Both bind $Ca^{2+}$ to regulate contraction
• Calmodulin is ubiquitous, Troponin C is muscle-specific

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: In a vascular smooth muscle biopsy, a drug prevents the phosphorylation of the myosin head despite adequate ATP and calcium-calmodulin complex formation. Which specific enzyme is being inhibited?
back:
• Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK)
• MLCK is the direct target of the $Ca^{2+}$-Calmodulin complex
• Inhibition prevents smooth muscle tone and contraction

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
coreConcept: Integration of Signaling in the Calmodulin System
front: Explain how the Calcium-Calmodulin system mediates the 'double signal' of membrane depolarization and hormone receptor activation to cause secretion.
back:
• Depolarization opens voltage-gated $Ca^{2+}$ channels
• Hormones open ligand-gated $Ca^{2+}$ channels
• Both raise cytosolic $Ca^{2+}$ to bind Calmodulin
• Activated Calmodulin-dependent kinases trigger exocytosis

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
coreConcept: Duration of Action: Calmodulin vs. cAMP
front: Contrast the persistence of the Calmodulin-dependent effect after calcium is removed with the immediate cessation seen in the cAMP system.
back:
• Calmodulin effects persist until protein phosphatases dephosphorylate the target proteins
• cAMP effects cease quickly due to rapid phosphodiesterase activity
• Calmodulin mediates longer-lasting physiological responses

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: How many specific binding sites for calcium ions must be occupied for Calmodulin to undergo the conformational change required for kinase activation?
back:
• Three to four (3-4) sites
• Binding causes the protein to 'wrap around' its target enzyme
• Partial binding is insufficient for full activation

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: The specific protein that undergoes a conformational change upon binding three to four calcium ions to initiate intracellular signaling is [___].
back:
• Calmodulin
• Acts as a regulatory protein after intracellular calcium levels rise
• Initiates multiple effects, including activation or inhibition of protein kinases.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: A researcher observes that a drug inhibiting Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK) prevents smooth muscle contraction. This indicates a block in the downstream effect of which intracellular second messenger system?
back:
• Calcium-Calmodulin Second Messenger System
• Calmodulin specifically activates MLCK
• MLCK then acts on smooth muscle myosin to induce contraction.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Explain the stoichiometric requirement and physical response of Calmodulin when intracellular calcium levels increase.
back:
• Requires binding of 3 to 4 calcium ions
• Upon binding, the protein changes its physical shape
• This conformational change allows it to interact with and activate/inhibit target protein kinases.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Contrast the calcium-sensing protein used in the contraction of vascular smooth muscle with that used in the contraction of the quadriceps muscle.
back:
• Smooth Muscle: Calmodulin (activates MLCK)
• Skeletal Muscle: Troponin C (moves tropomyosin)
• Both proteins are structurally and functionally similar but involve different downstream enzymes.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Identify the primary enzyme that converts a rise in intracellular calcium into a mechanical contraction in the gastrointestinal wall.
back:
• Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK)
• It is activated by the calcium-calmodulin complex
• It phosphorylates myosin to initiate cross-bridge cycling.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: While resting calcium concentration is $10^{-7}$ mol/L, the calcium-calmodulin system remains inactive until the concentration reaches [___] mol/L.
back:
• $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$ mol/L
• This 10- to 100-fold increase is required for sufficient binding
• Similar thresholds are seen in skeletal muscle Troponin C activation.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: A lab study shows a hormone receptor triggers calcium influx via voltage-gated channels. Describe the immediate biochemical step that follows calcium entry to ensure a cellular response.
back:
• Calcium binds to Calmodulin
• Calmodulin changes shape
• The complex activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinases via phosphorylation.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Explain how the Calcium-Calmodulin system achieves signal amplification within the cell after hormone-receptor interaction.
back:
• Initial calcium entry/release binds to Calmodulin
• Activated complex triggers calmodulin-dependent protein kinases
• Kinases phosphorylate multiple target proteins, amplifying the original hormonal signal.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Contrast the roles of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) and Calmodulin in the cellular response to hormones like Vasopressin (V1 receptor).
back:
• IP3: Mobilizes/releases calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum
• Calmodulin: Binds the released calcium to execute the final response (e.g., kinase activation)
• IP3 is the 'releaser,' Calmodulin is the 'sensor.'

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Name the specific protein found in the heart that serves as the structural and functional analogue to the endocrine system's Calmodulin.
back:
• Troponin C
• Both are calcium-binding regulatory proteins
• Both trigger a physiological response (contraction) only upon achieving specific calcium saturation.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: In the cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system, the enzyme [___] catalyzes the breakdown of phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2).
back:
● Phospholipase C (PLC)
● Cleaves PIP2 into two products: IP3 and DAG
● This enzyme is attached to the inside projections of transmembrane receptors.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: A woman in active labor receives an infusion to strengthen uterine contractions. The hormone administered (Oxytocin) carries out its function by activating which specific intracellular signaling pathway?
back:
● Cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
● Utilizes Phospholipase C (PLC)
● Increases intracellular calcium to promote smooth muscle contraction.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Explain the role of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) following its production by Phospholipase C in the hormonal signaling pathway.
back:
● Mobilizes calcium ions (Ca2+) from the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria
● Elevated cytosolic calcium initiates immediate cellular responses (e.g., secretion or contraction).

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Contrast the second messenger systems utilized by Vasopressin (ADH) at V1 receptors in vascular smooth muscle versus V2 receptors in the renal collecting tubules.
back:
● V1 Receptors: Phospholipase C (Phospholipid) system (IP3/DAG/Ca2+)
● V2 Receptors: Adenylyl Cyclase system (cAMP)
● V1 mediates vasoconstriction; V2 mediates water reabsorption.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Enlist the three hypothalamic releasing hormones that primarily utilize the Phospholipase C second messenger system.
back:
● Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH)
● Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
● Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH)

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Catecholamines utilize the Phospholipase C system when binding to [___] receptors, whereas they use the adenylyl cyclase system when binding to beta receptors.
back:
● Alpha (α) receptors (specifically α1)
● Activation leads to IP3-mediated calcium release
● Common in vascular smooth muscle contraction.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: A patient with severe hypotension is treated with Angiotensin II to increase blood pressure. Intracellularly, this hormone increases vascular resistance by activating [___].
back:
● Phospholipase C (PLC) / IP3-DAG system
● Increases intracellular calcium in vascular smooth muscle
● Results in potent vasoconstriction.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Describe how Diacylglycerol (DAG) functions as a second messenger and its link to local tissue hormones.
back:
● Activates Protein Kinase C (PKC) to phosphorylate target proteins
● DAG's lipid portion (arachidonic acid) acts as a precursor for prostaglandins and other local hormones.

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Distinguish between the two lipid-derived second messengers produced from phosphatidylinositol biphosphate (PIP2) regarding their immediate targets.
back:
● Inositol triphosphate (IP3): Targets intracellular calcium stores (ER/mitochondria)
● Diacylglycerol (DAG): Targets and activates Protein Kinase C (PKC).

category: Enumerate the hormones that use cell membrane phospholipid second messenger system
front: Enumerate the eight primary hormones or hormone-receptor pairings that utilize the cell membrane phospholipid (PLC) second messenger system.
back:
● Angiotensin II (Vascular SM)
● Catecholamines (α receptors)
● GnRH, GHRH, and TRH
● Parathyroid Hormone (PTH)
● Oxytocin
● Vasopressin (V1 receptor).

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: In the calcium-calmodulin second messenger system, a single calmodulin protein molecule must bind [___] calcium ions to undergo the conformational change required for activating intracellular protein kinases.
back:
• Four (4) calcium ions
• Binding to 3 or 4 sites triggers the shape change
• This activation enables the complex to initiate multiple cellular effects via protein kinases.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: A pharmacological agent is found to inhibit the phosphorylation of the Myosin Light Chain in vascular smooth muscle. This drug directly interferes with the enzymatic pathway typically activated by which intracellular calcium-binding protein complex?
back:
• Calcium-Calmodulin complex
• Normally activates Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK)
• This complex is essential for smooth muscle contraction via myosin phosphorylation.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Explain the sequence of events in the Calcium-Calmodulin system once intracellular calcium concentrations reach the activation threshold of $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-5}$ mol/L.
back:
• Calcium ions bind to calmodulin sites
• Calmodulin undergoes a conformational change
• The activated complex binds to and activates (or inhibits) specific protein kinases
• Kinase-mediated phosphorylation elicits the cellular response.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Contrast the regulatory role of the Calcium-Calmodulin system in smooth muscle with the Troponin-C system in skeletal muscle during the initiation of contraction.
back:
• Smooth Muscle: Calmodulin activates Myosin Light Chain Kinase; regulation is myosin-linked
• Skeletal Muscle: Troponin-C moves tropomyosin to expose actin sites; regulation is actin-linked
• Shared Feature: Both proteins have very similar structure and function.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Identify the two primary sources of calcium entry into the cytoplasm that trigger the calmodulin-dependent signaling pathway upon hormone-receptor interaction.
back:
• Influx of extracellular calcium through membrane channels (voltage or ligand-gated)
• Release of stored calcium from the endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum
• Initiation via changes in membrane potential or second messengers.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: The hypothalamic hormone responsible for inhibiting the secretion of growth hormone from the somatotropes is [___].
back:
• Somatostatin (Growth hormone inhibitory hormone/GHIH)
• It also inhibits the secretion of TSH to a lesser extent.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: A patient with a traumatic injury to the pituitary stalk exhibits high serum prolactin levels despite low levels of all other anterior pituitary hormones. This occurs due to the loss of [___].
back:
• Prolactin-inhibiting hormone (Dopamine)
• Loss of tonic hypothalamic inhibition allows lactotropes to secrete prolactin autonomously.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Explain the role of the 'pulsatile' secretion pattern of Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) in pituitary function.
back:
• Essential for maintaining sensitivity of gonadotropes
• Continuous GnRH exposure leads to receptor down-regulation
• Results in the suppression of LH and FSH secretion.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Contrast the effects of Growth Hormone–Releasing Hormone (GHRH) and Somatostatin on the pituitary gland's intracellular signaling.
back:
• GHRH: Stimulates adenylyl cyclase, increasing cAMP levels to trigger GH release.
• Somatostatin: Inhibits GH release by counteracting stimulatory signals at the somatotrope.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Identify the hypothalamic factor that stimulates both Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and Prolactin secretion.
back:
• Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH)
• While its primary target is the thyrotrope, it acts as a secondary stimulator for lactotropes.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: The primary hypothalamic peptide that stimulates the release of Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH) is [___].
back:
• Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)
• It is a 41-amino acid peptide that acts on pituitary corticotropes.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: A researcher discovers a hypothalamic lesion in a subject that results in failure of follicular development in the ovaries. This is most likely caused by a deficiency in [___].
back:
• Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
• Deficiency leads to insufficient LH and FSH production, which are critical for the ovarian cycle.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Explain the specific physiological route used by hypothalamic releasing factors to reach the anterior pituitary gland.
back:
• Secreted at nerve endings in the median eminence
• Absorbed into the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels
• Carried via blood to the glandular sinuses of the adenohypophysis.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Contrast the chemical structure of Prolactin-inhibiting hormone (PIH) with the other major hypothalamic releasing hormones.
back:
• PIH: An amine (Dopamine), derived from the amino acid tyrosine.
• Others: Most are peptides or polypeptides (e.g., TRH, CRH, GHRH, GnRH).

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Name the two hypothalamic hormones that are primarily synthesized in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei but released by the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Antidiuretic hormone (Vasopressin)
• Oxytocin
• Note: These are neurohormones rather than 'releasing factors'.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Intracellularly, the specific protein that possesses four binding sites for calcium and functions as a ubiquitous second messenger is [___].
back:
• Calmodulin.
• It undergoes a conformational change after binding 3–4 calcium ions.
• This change allows it to activate or inhibit various protein kinases.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: A physiological study observes smooth muscle contraction following an increase in cytosolic calcium. This effect is primarily mediated by the activation of [___].
back:
• Myosin Light Chain Kinase (MLCK).
• Triggered by the calcium-calmodulin complex.
• Results in phosphorylation of myosin heads to initiate contraction.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Explain the mechanical sequence that occurs once the intracellular calcium concentration reaches 10⁻⁶ mol/L.
back:
• Calcium binds to calmodulin sites.
• Calmodulin changes shape (conformational change).
• Complex activates/inhibits calmodulin-dependent protein kinases.
• Downstream proteins are phosphorylated to elicit a cellular response.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Contrast the regulatory role of Calmodulin in smooth muscle with its functional analog, Troponin-C, in skeletal muscle.
back:
• Smooth Muscle: Calmodulin activates MLCK to phosphorylate myosin.
• Skeletal Muscle: Troponin-C binds calcium to move tropomyosin off actin binding sites.
• Both share similar protein structures and calcium-binding affinities.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Identify the two primary triggers that initiate the entry of calcium into the cytoplasm to activate the calmodulin system.
back:
• Changes in membrane potential (opening voltage-gated calcium channels).
• Hormone-receptor interactions (opening ligand-gated or second-messenger-operated channels).

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Calmodulin-dependent protein kinases exert their intracellular effects on target proteins through the biochemical process of [___].
back:
• Phosphorylation.
• This process involves adding a phosphate group to specific amino acid residues.
• It serves to either activate or inhibit the target protein's function.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: A laboratory researcher notes that a cell remains inactive despite a calcium concentration of 10⁻⁸ mol/L. Provide the pathophysiological explanation for this lack of response.
back:
• 10⁻⁸ mol/L is the normal resting concentration.
• Calmodulin activation requires a rise to 10⁻⁶ or 10⁻⁵ mol/L.
• Insufficient calcium prevents the necessary conformational change in calmodulin.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: Describe how the calcium-calmodulin system differs from the Adenylyl Cyclase-cAMP system regarding the final enzymatic step.
back:
• cAMP system: Activates cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA).
• Calmodulin system: Activates calmodulin-dependent protein kinases (e.g., MLCK).
• Both systems utilize phosphorylation to modify cellular activity.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
coreConcept: IP3 vs Calmodulin in Calcium Signaling
front: Distinguish between the roles of Inositol Triphosphate (IP3) and Calmodulin in mediating calcium-related responses.
back:
• IP3: A messenger that mobilizes calcium from the ER/mitochondria.
• Calmodulin: A protein that binds the released calcium to execute signaling.
• IP3 acts upstream of the calcium-calmodulin binding event.

category: Explain the mechanism of calcium Calmodulin system
front: State the minimum number of calcium binding sites that must be occupied on a calmodulin molecule to trigger its functional activity.
back:
• Three or four sites.
• Calmodulin has a total of four calcium-binding sites.
• Sub-maximal binding fails to induce the required active conformation.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Approximately 30% to 40% of anterior pituitary cells are [___], which are responsible for the secretion of human growth hormone and stain strongly with acidic dyes.
back:
• Somatotropes (Acidophils).
• They are the most abundant cell type in the anterior pituitary.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: A 35-year-old female presents with a 'moon face,' 'buffalo hump,' and hypertension. Imaging reveals an anterior pituitary adenoma. Identify the specific cell type and hormone over-secreted in this patient.
back:
• Cell type: Corticotropes.
• Hormone: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH/Corticotropin).

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels in the delivery of releasing hormones to the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Releasing/inhibitory factors are secreted into the median eminence.
• These vessels carry the factors directly to the anterior pituitary sinuses.
• This allows local high concentrations to act on glandular cells.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Histology and Prevalence of Anterior Pituitary Cells
front: Contrast Somatotropes and Thyrotropes based on their staining characteristics and their relative percentages in the anterior pituitary gland.
back:
• Somatotropes: Acidophils; comprise 30% to 40% of cells.
• Thyrotropes: Basophils; comprise only 3% to 5% of cells.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the primary hypothalamic factor that maintains tonic inhibition over Prolactin secretion and name its chemical class.
back:
• Factor: Prolactin-inhibiting hormone (PIH).
• Chemical class: Dopamine (a catecholamine/amine).

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: The two glycoprotein hormones secreted by Gonadotropes that collectively regulate the maturation of germ cells and sex steroid production are [___] and [___].
back:
• Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH).
• Luteinizing hormone (LH).

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: A 40-year-old male presents with enlarging hands, protruding jaw (prognathism), and deepening of the voice. Which anterior pituitary hormone is chronically elevated in this patient, and what is its primary hepatic mediator?
back:
• Hormone: Growth Hormone (GH).
• Mediator: Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1 or Somatomedin C).

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: How does Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) acutely increase the release of thyroid hormones into the blood?
back:
• Binds to TSH receptors to activate the cAMP second messenger system.
• Triggers immediate proteolysis of thyroglobulin stored in follicles.
• This releases T3 and T4 into the circulation within 30 minutes.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the primary physiological stimulus for FSH versus LH in the male reproductive system.
back:
• FSH: Stimulates Sertoli cells for spermatogenesis.
• LH: Stimulates Leydig cells to secrete testosterone.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Name the specific embryological precursor of the anterior pituitary gland that distinguishes its epithelioid nature from the neural origin of the posterior pituitary.
back: • Rathke's pouch (an embryonic invagination of the pharyngeal epithelium).

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
coreConcept: Site of Synthesis of Posterior Pituitary Hormones
front: The hormones of the posterior pituitary are synthesized in the cell bodies of the [___] and [___] nuclei of the hypothalamus.
back:
• Supraoptic nuclei (primarily ADH)
• Paraventricular nuclei (primarily Oxytocin)
• Transported via axoplasm to the posterior pituitary for storage.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: A 25-year-old male presents with polyuria and polydipsia following a traumatic head injury that severed the pituitary stalk. The most likely hormone deficient in this patient is [___].
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) / Vasopressin
• Leads to Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Results in inability to concentrate urine.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of Neurophysins during the transport phase of neurohypophysial hormones.
back:
• Act as carrier proteins for ADH and Oxytocin
• Prevent hormone diffusion out of axons during transport
• Cleaved from hormones upon arrival at the posterior pituitary.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Contrast the primary hypothalamic nuclei responsible for ADH production versus those for Oxytocin production.
back:
• ADH: Primarily synthesized in the Supraoptic nuclei (approx. 5/6th).
• Oxytocin: Primarily synthesized in the Paraventricular nuclei (approx. 5/6th).
• Each nucleus can produce small amounts of the other hormone.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Enlist the two primary physiological stimuli that trigger the release of Antidiuretic Hormone into the blood.
back:
• Increased extracellular fluid osmolarity (detected by hypothalamic osmoreceptors)
• Decreased blood volume or low blood pressure (detected by arterial baroreceptors).

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: ADH facilitates water reabsorption by stimulating the insertion of water channels called [___] into the apical membranes of collecting duct cells.
back:
• Aquaporin-2
• Regulated via V2 receptors and the cAMP second messenger system
• Increases luminal permeability to water.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: A woman in active labor experiences strengthening contractions as the fetus's head stretches the cervix. Identify the hormone responsible for this positive feedback loop.
back:
• Oxytocin
• Stimulated by the Ferguson reflex (cervical stretch)
• Causes powerful rhythmic contractions of the uterine fundus.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Describe the mechanism of the 'Milk Ejection Reflex' (Milk Let-Down) initiated by an infant's suckling.
back:
• Suckling sends sensory signals to the hypothalamus
• Triggers oxytocin release from the posterior pituitary
• Oxytocin causes contraction of mammary myoepithelial cells.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Contrast the physiological effects of Vasopressin mediated by V1 receptors versus V2 receptors.
back:
• V1 Receptors: Mediate potent vasoconstriction of arterioles to increase blood pressure.
• V2 Receptors: Mediate water reabsorption in renal collecting tubules via cAMP.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Identify the embryological structure from which the posterior pituitary gland originates.
back:
• Neural tissue outgrowth from the hypothalamus (Neuroectoderm)
• Specifically the floor of the third ventricle
• Explains the presence of pituicytes (glial-like cells).

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: The carrier proteins that bind and transport hormones from the hypothalamic supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei down the axons to the posterior pituitary are called [___].
back:
• Neurophysins
  • They are synthesized with the hormone as a single protein chain
  • Hormones dissociate from them almost immediately after secretion into capillaries

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: A 25-year-old male presents with extreme polyuria (10L/day) and intense thirst after a head injury. Urinalysis shows a very low specific gravity. A deficiency in which posterior pituitary hormone is responsible for this pathophysiology?
back:
• Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) / Vasopressin
  • Diagnosis: Central Diabetes Insipidus
  • Pathophysiology: Failure of the collecting ducts to reabsorb water due to lack of ADH

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Explain the neuroendocrine mechanism of the 'milk let-down' reflex upon stimulation of the nipple.
back:
• Suckling sends sensory signals to the paraventricular and supraoptic nuclei
  • Oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary into the blood
  • Oxytocin causes contraction of mammary myoepithelial cells, expressing milk into ducts

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
coreConcept: Differential Stimuli of Posterior Pituitary Hormones
front: Contrast the primary physiological triggers and principal nuclear origins for the two hormones of the neurohypophysis.
back:
• ADH: Triggered by increased extracellular osmolarity; primarily synthesized in supraoptic nuclei
  • Oxytocin: Triggered by cervical stretch or suckling; primarily synthesized in paraventricular nuclei

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Enlist the two distinct vascular and renal effects of Vasopressin based on its specific receptor subtypes.
back:
• V1 Receptors: Constriction of arterioles (increases arterial pressure)
  • V2 Receptors: Increases water permeability of renal collecting tubules (via aquaporin-2 insertion)

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: The posterior pituitary gland, also referred to as the [___], is an extension of neural tissue and contains supporting glial-like cells called pituicytes.
back:
• Neurohypophysis
  • It stores and releases hormones but does not synthesize them
  • Synthesized hormones arrive via the hypothalamic-hypophysial tract

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: A woman in labor is administered a synthetic posterior pituitary hormone to induce delivery. This hormone facilitates birth by [___].
back:
• Oxytocin administration
  • Action: Stimulates powerful, rhythmic contractions of the pregnant uterine smooth muscle
  • Regulation: Often operates via a positive feedback mechanism during labor

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: The two primary hormones secreted by the posterior pituitary, which are actually synthesized in the hypothalamus, are [___] and [___].
back:
• Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) / Vasopressin
• Oxytocin
• Note: They are synthesized by magnocellular neurons.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: A 28-year-old female experiences difficulty during breastfeeding; milk is produced but fails to be expressed from the nipples upon suckling. This indicates a deficiency in the hormone [___].
back:
• Oxytocin
• Required for contraction of mammary myoepithelial cells surrounding alveoli
• Synthesized primarily in the paraventricular nucleus.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Explain the mechanism by which Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) increases water permeability in the renal collecting ducts.
back:
• Binds V2 receptors, activating adenylyl cyclase/cAMP
• Triggers phosphorylation of aquaporin-2 containing vesicles
• Promotes insertion of aquaporins into the apical cell membrane.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Contrast the primary hypothalamic nuclei responsible for the synthesis of Vasopressin versus Oxytocin.
back:
• Vasopressin (ADH): Synthesized primarily in the Supraoptic nucleus
• Oxytocin: Synthesized primarily in the Paraventricular nucleus
• Each nucleus can produce 1/6th of the other hormone.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Identify the carrier proteins that transport posterior pituitary hormones from the hypothalamus down the pituitary stalk.
back:
• Neurophysins
• Hormones and neurophysins are secreted together via exocytosis
• They dissociate almost immediately upon entering the blood.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: In states of significantly low blood volume (15-25% decrease), the posterior pituitary secretes high concentrations of ADH to produce a potent [___] effect.
back:
• Vasoconstrictor
• This action increases arterial pressure
• Mediated via V1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: A patient presents with extreme polyuria and dilute urine following a head injury that damaged the pituitary stalk. Explain why ADH levels would eventually return toward normal despite the damage.
back:
• Hormones are synthesized in the hypothalamus, not the pituitary
• Secretion can continue from the cut ends of fibers in the hypothalamus
• This follows a transient decrease of a few days.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Describe the Ferguson Reflex and the role of the posterior pituitary in labor.
back:
• Cervical stretching sends neurogenic signals to the hypothalamus
• Stimulates oxytocin release from the posterior pituitary
• Oxytocin increases uterine contractility via positive feedback.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Contrast the specific stimuli that trigger ADH secretion via osmoreceptors versus those involving atrial stretch receptors.
back:
• Osmoreceptors: Triggered by increased extracellular fluid osmolarity (cell shrinkage)
• Atrial stretch receptors: Triggered by low blood volume (underfilling)
• Osmotic stimuli are more sensitive.

category: Name the hormones of posterior pituitary
front: Why is the posterior pituitary considered a 'functional extension' of the hypothalamus rather than a true glandular organ?
back:
• It does not synthesize hormones; it stores and releases them
• Composed mainly of glial-like supporting cells (pituicytes)
• Composed of terminal nerve endings from hypothalamic neurons.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: The anterior pituitary gland, also known as the [___], is derived embryologically from Rathke’s pouch, an invagination of the pharyngeal epithelium.
back:
* Adenohypophysis
* Consists of epithelioid cells
* Secretes six major peptide hormones that regulate global metabolic functions

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: A patient is diagnosed with an acidophilic pituitary tumor causing excessive skeletal growth. Identify the specific hormone and cell type responsible.
back:
* Human Growth Hormone (hGH)
* Somatotropes
* Somatotropes constitute the largest cell population (30-40%) in the anterior pituitary

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Enlist the six major peptide hormones secreted by the adenohypophysis and their general chemical nature.
back:
* GH, ACTH, TSH, Prolactin, FSH, and LH
* All are either proteins, peptides, or glycoproteins
* Synthesized by five distinct cell types in the gland

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast the adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis regarding their embryological origins and primary modes of secretory control.
back:
* Adenohypophysis: Pharyngeal epithelium (Rathke's pouch); controlled by hypothalamic hormones via portal vessels
* Neurohypophysis: Neural tissue outgrowth; controlled by nerve signals from hypothalamic nuclei

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the two gonadotropic hormones of the anterior pituitary and the single hypothalamic hormone that stimulates their release.
back:
* Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing hormone (LH)
* Regulated by Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
* GnRH is secreted in pulsatile bursts from the arcuate nuclei

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: The anterior pituitary hormone primarily responsible for stimulating the production of glucocorticoids and androgens by the adrenal cortex is [___].
back:
* Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)
* Also called corticotropin
* Secreted by corticotropes, which comprise about 20% of anterior pituitary cells

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: A postpartum woman presents with a complete failure to produce milk. A deficiency in which anterior pituitary hormone and specific cell type is most likely?
back:
* Prolactin (PRL)
* Lactotropes (mammotropes)
* Prolactin is necessary for both mammary gland development and milk production

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Explain the role of Thyrotropes in metabolic regulation and the hormone they release.
back:
* Secrete Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
* Stimulates thyroid follicular cells to produce T3 and T4
* Controls the rates of most intracellular chemical reactions in the body

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Contrast Somatotropes and Corticotropes based on their relative abundance and the hormones they produce.
back:
* Somatotropes: Most abundant (30-40%); produce Growth Hormone (GH)
* Corticotropes: Second most abundant (~20%); produce Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH)

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Identify the unique hypothalamic factor that regulates Prolactin by primarily inhibiting its secretion.
back:
* Prolactin Inhibitory Hormone (PIH)
* Chemically identical to Dopamine
* Secreted by arcuate nuclei and carried via hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: The functional link between the hypothalamus and the anterior pituitary gland, where hypothalamic hormones are first secreted into the primary capillary plexus, is the [___].
back:
• Median eminence
• It connects the hypothalamus to the pituitary stalk
• Serves as the site for releasing/inhibitory hormone absorption into the portal system.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: A patient suffers a traumatic injury that severs the pituitary stalk. While levels of most anterior pituitary hormones fall, the serum level of [___] rises because it is no longer under tonic hypothalamic inhibition.
back:
• Prolactin
• Normally inhibited by Dopamine (Prolactin-Inhibiting Hormone)
• Disconnection removes this inhibitory signal, leading to hyperprolactinemia.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Explain the biological mechanism of hormone delivery from the hypothalamus to the systemic circulation via the posterior pituitary.
back:
• Synthesis: Occurs in cell bodies of magnocellular neurons (supraoptic/paraventricular nuclei).
• Transport: Conducted via axoplasm (hypothalamic-hypophysial tract) bound to neurophysins.
• Release: Secreted from nerve endings into capillaries by exocytosis.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Contrast the delivery systems used by the hypothalamus to regulate the anterior versus the posterior pituitary lobes.
back:
• Anterior: Vascular link via the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels (carrying releasing/inhibitory factors).
• Posterior: Neural link via the hypothalamic-hypophysial tract (carrying synthesized ADH and Oxytocin for storage).

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Identify the specific hypothalamic nuclei and cell types responsible for the primary synthesis of ADH and Oxytocin.
back:
• Cell type: Magnocellular neurons
• Supraoptic nuclei: Primarily synthesize ADH (Vasopressin)
• Paraventricular nuclei: Primarily synthesize Oxytocin.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Hormones from the hypothalamus reach the glandular cells of the adenohypophysis specifically through the [___].
back:
• Hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels
• This specialized vascular system prevents systemic dilution of hypothalamic hormones
• Allows rapid, high-concentration delivery to target anterior pituitary cells.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: A patient presents with extreme polyuria and dilute urine following neurosurgery. If the hypothalamic-hypophysial tract is damaged above the median eminence, identify the hormone deficiency and the resulting condition.
back:
• Hormone: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH/Vasopressin)
• Condition: Central Diabetes Insipidus
• Mechanism: Destruction of the neural tract prevents hypothalamic hormones from reaching the posterior pituitary release site.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: The functional anatomical link between the hypothalamus and the anterior pituitary gland, which allows the transport of releasing factors, is known as the [___].
back:
• Hypothalamic-hypophysial portal system.
• Consists of a primary capillary plexus in the median eminence.
• Portal vessels transport hormones directly to the adenohypophysis sinuses.
• Prevents dilution of hypothalamic factors in systemic blood.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: A patient suffers from a tumor compressing the pituitary stalk. Lab results show decreased levels of GH, TSH, and LH, but significantly elevated Prolactin. Identify the underlying pathophysiology.
back:
• Stalk compression blocks Prolactin-Inhibitory Hormone (Dopamine) from the hypothalamus.
• Unlike other hormones, Prolactin is under tonic inhibitory control.
• Loss of hypothalamic inhibition leads to autonomous lactotrope secretion.
• Other hormones decrease because their stimulatory releasing factors are blocked.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Explain the mechanism by which the hypothalamus regulates the release of hormones from the neurohypophysis.
back:
• Hormones (ADH/Oxytocin) are synthesized in supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
• Transported via axoplasm of the hypothalamic-hypophysial tract.
• Bound to carrier proteins called neurophysins during transport.
• Secreted by exocytosis from nerve endings directly into posterior pituitary capillaries.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Contrast the embryological origins of the anterior and posterior pituitary glands and describe how this dictates their different functional relationships with the hypothalamus.
back:
• Anterior: Derived from Rathke’s pouch (pharyngeal epithelium); connected via vascular portal vessels.
• Posterior: Derived from neural tissue outgrowth; connected via direct neural axonal tracts.
• This determines if control is via blood-borne releasing factors or direct electrical impulses.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Identify the primary role of the 'Median Eminence' in the regulation of metabolic functions.
back:
• Acts as the lowermost portion of the hypothalamus connecting to the pituitary stalk.
• Serves as the site where hypothalamic neurons secrete releasing and inhibitory hormones.
• Contains the primary capillary bed of the hypophysial portal system.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Large neurons in the hypothalamus that synthesize Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) and Oxytocin are clinically classified as [___] neurons.
back:
• Magnocellular neurons.
• Located specifically in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei.
• Their axons form the hypothalamic-hypophysial tract.
• Terminate in the posterior pituitary to release hormones into circulation.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: A female patient presents with secondary hypothyroidism due to hypothalamic failure. Predict the response of the anterior pituitary to an exogenous injection of Thyrotropin-Releasing Hormone (TRH).
back:
• Anterior pituitary (thyrotropes) will secrete TSH in response to TRH.
• Confirms the pituitary is functional but lacking hypothalamic stimulus.
• In primary hypothyroidism (gland failure), TSH would already be high due to loss of feedback.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Detail the biological importance of 'Pulsatile Secretion' in the relationship between the hypothalamus and the gonadotropes of the anterior pituitary.
back:
• GnRH must be released in intermittent pulses (every 90 minutes).
• Continuous GnRH infusion causes down-regulation/desensitization of pituitary receptors.
• Pulsatility is essential to maintain LH and FSH secretion and prevent hypogonadism.
• Frequency and quantity of pulses regulate different phases of the menstrual cycle.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Contrast the feedback oscillation loop of the Growth Hormone (GH) axis involving the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary.
back:
• GHRH (Hypothalamus) stimulates GH release from somatotropes.
• Somatostatin (GHIH) from the hypothalamus inhibits GH release.
• GH and Somatomedins (IGF-1) provide negative feedback by stimulating somatostatin and inhibiting GHRH.
• This maintains stable growth and metabolic rates.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Name the specific hypothalamic factor that exerts primary inhibitory control over the secretion of Prolactin.
back:
• Prolactin-Inhibiting Hormone (PIH).
• Chemically identical to the catecholamine Dopamine.
• Secreted by the arcuate nuclei into the portal system.
• Continuous inhibition is necessary to prevent inappropriate lactation in non-pregnant individuals.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: The hypothalamus is connected to the anterior pituitary gland through a specialized vascular network called the [___].
back: • Hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels. • These conduct releasing and inhibitory hormones from the median eminence. • Enables rapid, concentrated hormonal delivery to glandular cells.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: A patient suffers a traumatic injury that severs the hypophysial stalk. While most pituitary hormone levels drop, the serum concentration of Prolactin rises significantly. Explain the pathophysiology of this finding.
back: • Severing the stalk blocks Hypothalamic Prolactin Inhibitory Hormone (Dopamine). • The anterior pituitary is released from its tonic inhibition. • This 'stalk effect' leads to hyperprolactinemia.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Explain how hypothalamic neurosecretory cells regulate the secretion of hormones from the posterior pituitary gland.
back: • Hormones are synthesized in Supraoptic and Paraventricular nuclei. • Transported via axoplasm (Hypothalamic-hypophysial tract). • Stored in nerve endings; released by exocytosis upon neural stimulation.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Contrast the method of hormonal delivery from the hypothalamus to the anterior pituitary versus the delivery to the posterior pituitary.
back: • Anterior: Hormones travel via the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal blood system. • Posterior: Hormones travel via axons of the hypothalamic-hypophysial tract. • Delivery is vascular for the anterior and neural for the posterior.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Specify the embryological origins that dictate the functional difference between the adenohypophysis and the neurohypophysis.
back: • Adenohypophysis: Rathke's pouch (pharyngeal epithelium), consisting of epithelioid glandular cells. • Neurohypophysis: Neural tissue outgrowth from the hypothalamus, consisting of glial-type pituicytes and nerve fibers.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: The functional link between the hypothalamus and the anterior pituitary gland, where hypothalamic neurons release their factors into the primary capillary plexus, is the [___].
back: • Median eminence. • It connects inferiorly with the pituitary stalk. • Small arteries coalesce here to form the portal vessels.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: An experimental study involves stimulating the paraventricular nucleus (PVN) of the hypothalamus. Identify the two hormones primarily released into either the systemic circulation or portal system as a result.
back: • Oxytocin (into posterior pituitary systemic blood). • Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH) (into hypothalamic-hypophysial portal system). • PVN contains both magnocellular and parvocellular neurons.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Describe the transport and storage mechanism of hormones moving from the hypothalamus to the neurohypophysis.
back: • Hormones bind to carrier proteins called neurophysins. • Move via axoplasmic flow down the pituitary stalk. • Stored in terminal bulbous knobs until nerve impulses trigger release.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Contrast the secretory cells of the anterior pituitary with the 'secretory' components found in the posterior pituitary.
back: • Anterior: Contains intrinsic glandular cells (somatotropes, thyrotropes, etc.). • Posterior: Lacks intrinsic glandular cells; contains terminal nerve endings of hypothalamic neurons. • Posterior serves only as a storage and release site.

category: Describe the functional relationship between hypothalamus, anterior and posterior pituitary gland
front: Name the major hypothalamic hormone that, unlike others, primarily exerts a tonic inhibitory effect on its target anterior pituitary cells.
back: • Prolactin Inhibitory Hormone (PIH). • Biochemically identified as Dopamine. • Secreted by neurons in the arcuate nuclei into the portal system.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), which stimulates the secretion of GH by somatotropes, is primarily synthesized in the [___] nucleus of the hypothalamus.
back:
* Arcuate nucleus.
* Also produced in the ventromedial nucleus.
* Secreted into the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels to reach the anterior pituitary.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: A 32-year-old female with primary hypothyroidism (low T3/T4) presents with galactorrhea. Explain the underlying pathophysiology involving hypothalamic factors.
back:
* Lack of thyroid hormone feedback increases hypothalamic Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH).
* TRH stimulates both thyrotropes (TSH) and lactotropes.
* Excessive TRH causes hyperprolactinemia, leading to inappropriate milk production.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Describe the intracellular mechanism by which Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) carries out its function in the anterior pituitary.
back:
* Binds to TRH receptors on pituitary cell membranes.
* Activates the phospholipase C second messenger system.
* Increases calcium ions and diacylglycerol (DAG) to trigger hormone release.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
coreConcept: GHRH vs Somatostatin in GH Pathology
front: A patient presents with symptoms of acromegaly. Contrast the hypothalamic hormonal profile expected if the condition is caused by a GHRH-secreting ectopic tumor versus a primary somatotrope adenoma.
back:
* GHRH-secreting tumor: Elevated plasma GHRH levels; causes somatotrope hyperplasia.
* Primary adenoma: Low GHRH due to negative feedback by GH/IGF-1; elevated hypothalamic Somatostatin.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Enumerate the specific hypothalamic factors that exert an inhibitory rather than a releasing effect on the anterior pituitary gland.
back:
* Somatostatin (Growth Hormone Inhibitory Hormone).
* Dopamine (Prolactin Inhibitory Hormone).
* Somatostatin also provides minor inhibitory control over TSH secretion.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: In the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, the peptide consisting of 41 amino acids that is the primary trigger for ACTH release is [___].
back:
* Corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH).
* Synthesized primarily in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN).
* Secreted into the primary capillary plexus of the median eminence.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: A researcher administers a continuous, non-pulsatile infusion of GnRH to a subject. Describe the resulting effect on LH/FSH levels and the underlying cellular cause.
back:
* Plasma LH and FSH levels fall significantly.
* Continuous exposure causes down-regulation of GnRH receptors.
* Pituitary gonadotropes become desensitized to the hypothalamic stimulus.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Explain the mechanism by which the hypothalamus regulates TSH during exposure to severe cold and identify the neural pathway involved.
back:
* Cold excites hypothalamic centers for body temperature control.
* Increases TRH secretion into the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal system.
* TRH can increase thyroid hormone output to 100% above normal.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Contrast Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) and Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) regarding their chemical chain lengths and target cell specificity.
back:
* TRH: Tripeptide (3 amino acids); targets thyrotropes and lactotropes.
* GnRH: Decapeptide (10 amino acids); targets gonadotropes.
* Both are peptides transported via the hypophysial portal blood.

category: Name the hormones/ factors of hypothalamus
front: Identify the only hypothalamic inhibitory factor that is an amine (catecholamine) and the specific hypothalamic nuclei that produce it.
back:
* Prolactin-inhibiting hormone (PIH), also known as Dopamine.
* Produced by the arcuate nuclei.
* Tonic secretion keeps Prolactin levels low in non-pregnant/non-nursing individuals.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: The hypothalamic hormones intended for the anterior pituitary are released into the [___] capillary plexus located in the median eminence.
back:
• Primary
• This plexus is the entry point for releasing/inhibitory factors into the portal system.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: A patient suffers a severe head injury that severs the pituitary stalk. Laboratory results show decreased levels of ACTH, TSH, and GH, but significantly elevated Prolactin. Explain the physiological cause for the rise in Prolactin.
back:
• Interruption of Prolactin Inhibitory Hormone (Dopamine) transport
• Dopamine normally travels via portal vessels to suppress lactotropes
• Loss of inhibitory control leads to spontaneous hyperprolactinemia.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Explain the significance of the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal system regarding hormone concentration and dilution.
back:
• Provides direct transport pathway
• Prevents dilution of hypothalamic hormones in the systemic circulation
• Ensures high local concentrations for immediate pituitary receptor activation.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Contrast the vascular connection of the adenohypophysis with the neural connection of the neurohypophysis.
back:
• Adenohypophysis: Hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels (hormonal control)
• Neurohypophysis: Hypothalamic-hypophysial tract (axonal transport of ADH and Oxytocin).

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Identify the specific anatomical structures through which hypothalamic releasing hormones must pass between the median eminence and the anterior pituitary sinuses.
back:
• Hypothalamic-hypophysial portal blood vessels
• These vessels descend along the pituitary stalk (infundibulum).

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: In the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal system, the secondary capillary plexus consists of extensive [___] located among the glandular cells of the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Sinuses
• These allow for the rapid exchange of hormones between blood and endocrine cells.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: A 40-year-old male with a non-functioning pituitary macroadenoma presents with low testosterone levels. Describe the mechanism of this hormonal deficiency in relation to hypothalamic communication.
back:
• Tumor mass effect compresses portal vessels
• Blocks GnRH transport to the anterior pituitary
• Resulting lack of LH/FSH prevents testosterone production by Leydig cells.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Detail the step-wise route of a Thyrotropin-Releasing Hormone (TRH) molecule from its site of secretion to its target cell.
back:
• Secreted by hypothalamic neurons into median eminence interstitial fluid
• Absorbed into primary capillary plexus
• Carried via hypophysial portal vessels to anterior pituitary sinuses
• Binds to thyrotrope receptors.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Distinguish between the primary capillary plexus and the secondary capillary plexus of the hypophysial portal system by location.
back:
• Primary: Located in the median eminence (lower hypothalamus)
• Secondary: Located within the sinuses of the anterior pituitary gland.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Explain why almost all anterior pituitary hormone levels fall to baseline when the pituitary gland is transplanted to a distant site in the body.
back:
• Loss of the specialized hypothalamic-hypophysial portal connection
• Hypothalamic releasing hormones cannot reach the gland in sufficient concentrations via systemic blood.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Embryological Origin of the Anterior Pituitary
front: The anterior pituitary gland, responsible for secreting six major metabolic hormones, is embryologically derived from an upward invagination of the pharyngeal epithelium known as [___].
back:
• Rathke’s pouch.
• This origin explains the epithelioid nature of its cells.
• Distinct from the neurohypophysis, which originates from neural tissue.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Anterior Pituitary Cell Types and Hormones
front: A 35-year-old female presents with cold intolerance, weight gain, and fatigue. Clinical labs reveal low T3/T4 and inappropriately low TSH levels. Identify the specific anterior pituitary cell type failing to function.
back:
• Thyrotropes.
• These cells constitute approximately 3% to 5% of the anterior pituitary.
• They secrete Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH).

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Describe the mechanism by which hypothalamic hormones regulate the secretory activity of specific glandular cells in the adenohypophysis.
back:
• Secretion into the median eminence tissue fluids.
• Transport via hypothalamic-hypophysial portal blood vessels.
• Binding to specific surface receptors on anterior pituitary glandular cells.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
coreConcept: Diabetogenic Effects of Anterior Pituitary Hormones
front: In a patient presenting with secondary hyperglycemia, contrast the metabolic mechanisms by which excessive Growth Hormone (GH) and excessive ACTH-induced Cortisol contribute to elevated blood glucose.
back:
• GH: Induces "insulin resistance," decreasing glucose uptake in muscle and adipose tissue.
• Cortisol: Increases hepatic gluconeogenesis and inhibits insulin-mediated glucose transport.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: Name the hypothalamic neurotransmitter that pharmacologically acts as the primary tonic inhibitor of prolactin secretion from the anterior pituitary.
back:
• Dopamine.
• Also known as Prolactin-inhibiting hormone (PIH).
• Secreted by the arcuate nuclei of the hypothalamus.

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: In the histological identification of anterior pituitary cells, the presence of [___] staining is the specific criterion used to classify somatotropes and lactotropes.
back:
• Acidophilic (Acidophils).
• They stain strongly with acidic dyes.
• Somatotropes are the most abundant cell type (30-40%).

category: Name the hormones of anterior pituitary
front: A 45-year-old male presents with broadening of the nose, protruding supraorbital ridges, and an increase in shoe size. Identify the hormone responsible and the specific condition if epiphyseal fusion has already occurred.
back:
• Growth Hormone (GH).
• Condition: Acromegaly.
• Characterized by thickening of membranous bones and soft tissue enlargement.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: The hypothalamic releasing and inhibitory hormones reach the anterior pituitary gland through a specialized vascular network known as the [___].
back:
• Hypothalamic-hypophysial portal vessels.
• Transports neurohormones from the median eminence to the adenohypophysis.
• Prevents systemic dilution of hypothalamic factors.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: A patient develops a tumor that compresses the infundibular stalk, severing the portal blood supply. Contrast the expected change in Prolactin levels with that of Growth Hormone.
back:
• Prolactin: Rises (hyperprolactinemia) due to loss of hypothalamic Dopamine inhibition.
• Growth Hormone: Decreases due to loss of GHRH stimulation.
• This is called the 'stalk effect.'

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Explain the sequence of hormone transport from hypothalamic neurons to the anterior pituitary secretory cells.
back:
• Hormones are secreted into tissue fluids of the median eminence.
• Absorbed into the primary capillary plexus.
• Carried via portal vessels to the secondary capillary sinuses (adenohypophysis).

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
front: Contrast the delivery route of Oxytocin and Vasopressin with that of Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH).
back:
• Oxytocin/Vasopressin: Transported via axoplasm (neural tract) to the posterior pituitary.
• GnRH: Transported via the hypothalamic-hypophysial portal circulation to the anterior pituitary.

category: Explain the significance of hypothalamic- hypophysial portal circulation
